That reading is the hymn's own (see phelps-hie-to-kolob-1856-q1, where the quatrain is tagged BACKWARD-AGNOSTIC for the same reason), and it is worth noting that Lee reaches for it three paragraphs after defending the King Follett statement — the same address holds the claim and the prohibition on pressing it further. MANY-WORLDS for "worlds and lives abound." Deliberately not tagged DIVINE-PROGRESSION: "Improvement and progression Have one eternal round" is a claim about the universe, not about God, per the note on phelps-hie-to-kolob-1856-q3. Lee prints the older "D'ye think that you could ever" wording and cites the hymn as no. 257; it is no. 284 in the 1985 hymnal.

quotes.excerpt: A prophet-leader of our dispensation then extends this great wisdom to all truth seekers: "Many have tried to penetrate to the First Cause of all things; but it would be as easy for an ant to number the grains of sand on the earth. It is not for man, with his limited intelligence, to grasp eternity in his comprehension. . . . What, then, should be the calling and duty of the children of men? Instead of inquiring after the origin of the Gods — instead of trying to explore the depths of eternities that have been, that are, and that will be, — instead of endeavoring to discover the boundaries of boundless space, let them seek to know the object of their present existence, and how to apply, in the most profitable manner for their mutual good and salvation, the intelligence they possess. . . ." (Brigham Young, in Journal of Discourses, Vol. 7, p. 284.)
quotes.note: Young's October 9, 1859 caution (young-origin-caution-1859) reissued from the general conference pulpit 110 years later, and introduced as "this great wisdom." This is the transmission line the 1859 entry's note predicted: the caution survives in usage while the chain language it was delivered alongside does not. Lee's Conference Report prints the Americanised "endeavoring"; the Journal of Discourses reads "endeavouring."

quotes.excerpt: The ancient prophet was not speaking idly when he declared in exaltation, "O how great the holiness of our God! For he knoweth all things, and there is not anything save he knows it." (2 Ne. 9:20.)
quotes.note: Recorded untagged on purpose. This is a full-omniscience assertion, and full omniscience is the premise Joseph Fielding Smith would use two years later to rule out progression in knowledge (jfs-progression-1971), and that the 2002 institute manual uses for the same purpose (dcsm-2002-omniscience). But Lee draws no such inference: he is not addressing whether God progresses, and the next sentence turns to "a state of ultimate perfection to which all might attain" — the subject is man's attainment, not God's stasis. Tagging DIVINE-PROGRESSION here would be reading the later debate back into a doxological line, which is precisely what the no-retrojection rule forbids. The observation belongs in the note, and it is made here so a later reader does not mistake the silence for an oversight.

quotes.excerpt: The wisdom of the teacher's reply to the young men in Chicago is impressed by another statement from a modern prophet: "These are incomprehensible ideas to some, but they are simple. It is the first principle of the gospel to know for a certainty the character of God, and to know that we may converse with Him as one man converses with another. . . ." (DHC, Vol. 6, p. 305.)
quotes.note: A textual datum worth having on the record. Lee's ellipsis falls exactly where the King Follett text continues "and that he was once a man like us; yea, that God himself, the Father of us all, dwelt on an earth, the same as Jesus Christ himself did." He stops one clause short of the mortality claim. This is not suppression — Lee has already defended that claim in his own voice earlier in the same address (q1) — but it is the standard mid-century citation habit, and it is worth setting beside cullimore-character-of-god-1970-q1, where the identical sentence is printed eighteen months later with the clause intact. Lee also quotes DHC 6:306–7 elsewhere in the address (the ladder passage on learning "all the principles of exaltation"), naming it "King Follett Discourse"; that is the second of the two explicit citation edges to kfd-1844.

notes: Re-read in full and quoted verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1969/1969-04-lee-in-the-spirit-of-that-beautiful-hymn.md, whose final-review pass independently re-collated leaves n131–n135 of the Church History Library preservation scan (Internet Archive conferencereport1969a) with reading order rebuilt from the scan's DjVu word coordinates and found the body already clean. Conference Report, so hearsay A; the two Journal of Discourses passages and the two Documentary History passages quoted inside it are relays and are graded in their quote notes. Filed sourceType original, not citation: Lee is answering a live question with an argument of his own, and the quoted material is his evidence rather than the entry's whole content. Why this entry matters. It is the fullest single-address demonstration in the dataset that the backward claim and the prohibition on pursuing it were held together rather than in sequence: within about a thousand words Lee defends "God was once as we are now" as literally true, adds Brigham Young's "has had a body and been on an earth," glosses D&C 131's "increase" with Young's "father of fathers … by the increase of his own progeny," and then quotes both "If You Could Hie to Kolob" and Young's "instead of inquiring after the origin of the Gods" to close the question off. Two years before the Ensign reprinted the King Follett Sermon whole (ensign-king-follett-1971), an apostle was defending it from the pulpit against a member who could not accept it — and telling the same congregation not to go further back. Context flag carried from the vault file: President Joseph Fielding Smith's address from the same session was never ingested into the corpus, so no comparison with it is offered here.

title: Relief Society theology lesson: the “eternal round” of spirit children born to exalted beings
speaker: Roy W. Doxey
office: Writer of the Relief Society Magazine theology lessons (styled “Elder Roy W. Doxey” in the lesson heading)
venue: “Lesson 97—Eternal Marriage,” Lesson Department, The Relief Society Magazine 56, no. 7 (July 1969): 540–545

quotes.excerpt: The children born to an exalted man and woman after the resurrection are spirit beings. The parents are tangible, resurrected persons referred to in the scriptures as having spiritual bodies; that is, with spirit element in their veins rather than blood as in mortal bodies. (D&C 88:27; Al. 11:45; Brigham Young, Discourses of Brigham Young, p. 374.)
quotes.note: Printed p. 543, under the heading “Eternal Increase.” Explicit on both axes the taxonomy separates. Forward: exalted couples have children after the resurrection and those children are spirits. Mechanism: the lesson does not leave the physiology alone, but supplies it — the parents are tangible resurrected persons with “spirit element in their veins rather than blood,” the Brigham Young account of how resurrected bodies can beget spirits, cited to Discourses of Brigham Young. That is spirit-matter physiology in the Pratt–Young line, so SPIRIT-BIRTH-VIVIPAROUS applies; what it stops short of is gestation or sexual language, which the lesson never uses.

quotes.excerpt: In the premortal world the plan of salvation was formed whereby the spirit sons and daughters of God could receive an earth life necessary for eternal progression. The relationship between God and his children was a parent-child relationship because his spirit children were born of a Heavenly Father and Heavenly Mother. (Harold B. Lee, Youth and the Church, pp. 126-27.) The eternal round of spirit children being born to exalted beings and the opportunity to reach the heights of exaltation by an earth life require marriage for eternity by mortals.
quotes.note: Printed p. 545, under the heading “Implementation.” Heavenly Mother is stated as the reason the divine parent-child relationship is what it is, not offered as a devotional aside, and the authority cited is a sitting apostle's book (Harold B. Lee, Youth and the Church). On the forward chain: the lesson names the round and names the exaltation route, but it does not say in terms that the spirit children born to exalted beings will themselves receive worlds and become gods. The whole weight of that claim rests on the word “round,” and the sentence's grammar leaves “the opportunity to reach the heights of exaltation by an earth life” attached to mortals generally rather than specifically to the newly born spirits. So the closed forward chain is implied by the vocabulary and is not asserted — recorded here, deliberately, as implication rather than as text.

notes: Verified verbatim against the archive.org page images of printed pp. 543 and 545 (item reliefsocietymag56reli, IA leaves 565 and 567), collated against the item's full text. This is the answer to the open question the archival sweep left: the lesson is “Lesson 97—Eternal Marriage” by Roy W. Doxey, in the Lesson Department of the July 1969 issue, printed pp. 540–545, with the reading assignment D&C 131:1–4 and 132, and headed for use in the first meeting of October 1969 (Northern Hemisphere) or March 1970 (Southern). The sweep's provisional B3 upgrade should not be made: the lesson is unambiguous B2 with stated physiology, and the forward chain beyond that is carried only by the phrase “eternal round” — see the note on q2. Two further passages set the register. On p. 543 the lesson glosses D&C 132:24–25 as “eternal lives, the power of eternal increase, which is the opposite of the deaths, or the lack of such power.” And the whole lesson is built on quoted authorities rather than on its own voice — Joseph Smith, Brigham Young, Joseph F. Smith, Widtsoe, McKay, Melvin J. Ballard, and Harold B. Lee — which is what makes it useful evidence about what was safe to teach women in 1969 rather than merely about what one lesson writer thought. Filed historical-official: an official auxiliary magazine's correlated lesson course, no longer published.

title: Sterling W. Sill: “God, angels, spirits, and men are all of the same species”
speaker: Sterling W. Sill
office: Assistant to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, first day morning session, Salt Lake Tabernacle (Conference Report, October 1969; Internet Archive scan conferencereport1969sa, leaf n18)

quotes.excerpt: It is helpful for us to remember that God, angels, spirits, and men are all of the same species in different stages of development and in various degrees of righteousness.
quotes.note: A species-identity claim, not a bare "we may become like God": God and men are asserted to be one kind, distinguished only by stage of development and degree of righteousness. The tag is a judgment call and is flagged as such. What earns it is that the developmental scale is predicated of a list with God on it, which places God at a stage rather than outside the sequence; what holds the stance at "hedges" is that Sill never says God attained that stage, never says he was once mortal, and is not, in context, discussing God's origin at all — the paragraph is about seeing fellow worshippers in "the light of their real identity as children of God." Referent must stay ambiguous: "God" is unqualified here, and the address nowhere pins the word to the Father as against Christ. Bare theosis carries no tag in this scheme, so a reader should not take the pill as evidence that Sill taught the backward claim; the note is the finding.

notes: Re-read in full and quoted verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1969/1969-10-sill-if-we-were-looking-for-some-program.md, independently collated at final review against leaf n18 of the Church History Library preservation scan (Internet Archive conferencereport1969sa). Conference Report, so A. Deliberately lean: the address is a Sabbath-observance sermon, and the ontology surfaces in a single aside under the printed side-head "Rewarding Associations," alongside the claim that "the most ordinary individual that we know may be the kind of person that we would feel like falling down and worshiping before." The sentence is nonetheless worth a row, because the same-species formulation is the ontological premise the whole dataset turns on, and this is it stated flatly, in general conference, in 1969, with no argument offered and none apparently thought necessary. Note that Sill supplies no source for it; the formulation echoes the nineteenth-century scale-of-intelligence language (compare pratt-heirship-intelligence-1853-q3) rather than any scripture he cites.

title: Victor L. Brown: seminary students “had existed as intelligences and then as spirit children”
speaker: Victor L. Brown
office: Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric
venue: General conference, third day afternoon session, Salt Lake Tabernacle (Conference Report, October 1969; Internet Archive scan conferencereport1969sa, leaves n134–n135)

quotes.excerpt: It was interesting to note that these young people were thrilled with the knowledge that they had existed as intelligences and then as spirit children of their Heavenly Father before they were born into this life.
quotes.note: Three stages, named in order, in one sentence: intelligences, then spirit children of the Father, then birth into this life. This is what the category actually requires — real intelligence → spirit → body staging rather than the two-stage eternalism that gets retrojected onto Abraham 3 and the King Follett Discourse. Two things make it more than a one-speaker datum. It is reported as what fifteen-year-olds had been taught in a seminary class and could recite back with enthusiasm, so it is evidence about correlated curriculum in 1969, not about Brown's private view; and the tripartite frame is stated with no mechanism whatever for the intelligence-to-spirit-child transition, which is the shape the model usually takes in this period. Because no begetting is described, neither SPIRIT-BIRTH tag applies.

quotes.excerpt: It is my testimony that every person born into this world is a spirit child of God, that we did in very deed live with our Heavenly Father before taking a mortal body.
quotes.note: Brown's own voice, and it is two-stage: spirit child, then mortal body, with the intelligences dropped. Recorded so the entry shows where the three-stage frame actually sits — in the reported seminary lesson of q1, not in the apostolic-office testimony that follows it. No mechanism is offered for how one becomes a spirit child, so nothing on the spirit-birth axis is tagged.

notes: Re-read in full and quoted verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1969/1969-10-brown-my-brethren-and-sisters-i-am-grate.md, whose final-review pass re-collated leaves n134–n135 of the Church History Library preservation scan (Internet Archive conferencereport1969sa), reconstructed a two-column OCR interleave in the opening paragraph, and trimmed a large block of unrelated matter (David O. McKay's closing address and the conference back matter) that had been absorbed into the file's tail; the passages quoted here sit inside Brown's own body text, well before that boundary. Conference Report, so A. This is Bishop Victor L. Brown of the Presiding Bishopric, not President Hugh B. Brown, who also spoke at this conference. A lean entry by design: the address is about eternal life and agency, and the tripartite sentence is an aside — which is exactly why it is useful as a measure of what the model's ordinary, unremarkable statement looked like in 1969.

title: Bruce R. McConkie: “one of our great doctrinal hymns”
speaker: Bruce R. McConkie
office: Of the First Council of the Seventy
venue: General conference, second session, Saturday afternoon (Conference Report, April 1970)

quotes.excerpt: In one of our great doctrinal hymns we sing: "In the heavens are parents single? No; the thought makes reason stare! Truth is reason, truth eternal Tells me I've a mother there. "When I leave this frail existence, When I lay this mortal by, Father, Mother, may I meet you In your royal courts on high? Then, at length, when I've completed All you sent me forth to do, With your mutual approbation Let me come and dwell with you." —Hymns, No. 138
quotes.note: “One of our great doctrinal hymns” — the classification is the datum. McConkie, who spent a career policing the boundary between doctrine and folklore, files the Heavenly Mother stanzas on the doctrine side without qualification, and opens the talk with them. The hymnal number McConkie gives is 138, from the book then in use; Gordon B. Hinckley will cite the same lines as no. 292 from the 1985 hymnal in 1991 — the numbering is a cheap dating check on any later quotation of the hymn. Verse line breaks rendered as running text; the stray opening quotation mark before “When I leave” is in the printed Report.

quotes.excerpt: Manifestly if we are to become like our Eternal Father, we must become immortal as he is immortal; we must gain the character, perfections, and attributes which he possesses; we must attain the power, glory, and dominion which he enjoys; and we must create for ourselves eternal family units patterned after his eternal family.
quotes.note: The euphemism in its mature form, and it is doing real work: “create for ourselves eternal family units patterned after his eternal family” says everything the older sources said about generative exaltation except the word children. The pattern claim also runs backward by implication — his family is the template — but McConkie asserts nothing about the Father's own origin here, so no backward tag.

quotes.excerpt: Full salvation consists of the continuation of the family unit in celestial glory… heaven itself is but the projection of a Latter-day Saint family into eternity… That power by which salvation comes is so great that it can make of earth a heaven, and of man, a god.
quotes.note: The closing formulation, with two elisions marked. “Continuation of the family unit” is D&C 132's “continuation of the seeds” with the biology removed — compare hunter-beget-spirit-children-1949 twenty-one years earlier, where the same verse is glossed as “the power to beget spirit children.” Same doctrine, same scripture, and in the interval the mechanism has gone silent while the promise (“of man, a god”) has not.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1970/1970-04-mcconkie-salvation-is-a-family-affair.md, whose Final Review collated the full body against the archive.org scan conferencereport1970a, leaves n27–n30, word for word, with no lexical fixes needed; seven bled-in printed side-heads were converted to Markdown headings and trailing material belonging to the following speaker was stripped in an earlier pass. One shared OCR artifact survives elsewhere in the talk (“prepare arid qualify us”), reproduced identically by the independent witness and therefore left alone; it does not touch any quoted excerpt. Conference Report, so A; historical-official. Filed as a citation because the entry's Heavenly Mother content is the hymn — McConkie adds no argument about her, and the talk's own argument is about the family unit — but the two euphemism quotes are carried because this is McConkie establishing the vocabulary he will police for the next two decades. Read against mcconkie-heresies-1980 and mcconkie-mormon-doctrine.

title: James A. Cullimore reads the King Follett material twice: the God who makes a “literal Father in heaven” intelligible
speaker: James A. Cullimore
office: Assistant to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, first day afternoon session, Salt Lake Tabernacle (Conference Report, October 1970; Internet Archive scan conferencereport1970sa, leaf n42)

quotes.excerpt: The Prophet Joseph Smith taught, "It is the first principle of the Gospel to know for a certainty the Character of God, and to know that we may converse with him as one man converses with another, and that he was once a man like us; yea, that God himself, the Father of us all, dwelt on an earth, the same as Jesus Christ himself did." (Teachings of the Prophet Joseph Smith, pp. 345-46.)
quotes.note: The same sentence Harold B. Lee cut short with an ellipsis eighteen months earlier (lee-true-concept-of-god-1969-q8), here printed whole, mortality clause and all, in the Conference Report. The referent is explicit in the text — "God himself, the Father of us all" — which is why this is one of the cleaner Father-referent attestations in the correlated era. Hearsay C for this quote: Teachings of the Prophet Joseph Smith is a 1938 compilation drawing on the Documentary History amalgam of the four King Follett witnesses, not an independent report of what was said in 1844; see kfd-1844.

quotes.excerpt: The kind of a God as described by the Prophet Joseph Smith makes me understand him as my literal Father in heaven. He said: "God himself was once as we are now, and is an exalted man, and sits enthroned in yonder heavens! That is the great secret. If the veil were rent today, and the great God, who holds this world in its orbit, and who holds all worlds and all things by His power, was to make himself visible — I say, if you were to see him today, you would see him like a man in form — like yourselves in all the person, image, and very form as a man…" (Documentary History of the Church, vol. 6, p. 305.)
quotes.note: Both halves of the Father-status axis in one sentence — past mortality ("was once as we are now") and attainment ("is an exalted man") — so both tags, per the precedent set on kfd-1844-q1 and ensign-king-follett-1971-q2. The framing clause is the entry's own contribution and is quoted with the passage on purpose: Cullimore offers the King Follett God not as a mystery to be handled carefully but as the thing that makes God pastorally intelligible, "my literal Father in heaven." Hearsay C: the Documentary History reading is the smoothed amalgam, not any of the four contemporaneous witnesses.

quotes.excerpt: It is man's purpose in life to learn to know God, to know the nature and kind of being God is, and then to conform to his laws and ordinances; to progress, to be exalted to that high state wherein man becomes perfect as the Father is perfect.
quotes.note: The forward direction as Cullimore leaves it: bare theosis on the Matthew 5:48 model, with no increase, no offspring, no worlds, and no "eternal lives." Untagged, because plain likeness-to-God carries no tag in this scheme. Recorded because it shows where the address's weight actually falls — everything radical in it is backward-facing, and the forward half is the mildest available formula.

notes: Re-read in full and quoted verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/conference-reports/1970/1970-10-cullimore-my-brethren-and-sisters-how-de-esting.md, whose final-review pass collated the body word for word against the Church History Library preservation scan (Internet Archive conferencereport1970sa, reading order reconstructed, leaves 40–43) and re-verified the prior de-interleaving of a two-column OCR garble in the opening sentence. The Conference Report is A; the two Joseph Smith quotations inside it are Documentary History / Teachings amalgams and are downgraded to C per quote. Filed as a citation of kfd-1844, on the abrea-same-as-all-gods-1981 precedent: the address's doctrinal content on this axis is the two quoted passages, and Cullimore's own addition is a frame rather than an argument. What the entry documents. In October 1970 — the last conference before the Ensign began, the year before Joseph Fielding Smith's First Presidency message denying that God progresses (jfs-progression-1971), and in the middle of Correlation — an Assistant to the Twelve built a general conference address on the nature of God around the King Follett statement, quoted it twice from two different compilations, and treated it as the ordinary answer to a schoolchild's question about how to draw God. No hedge, no caveat, no counsel to leave it alone. The rest of the address is about the personality of God as a precondition for revelation, worked out through William E. Berrett's 1941 contrast with Henry Wieman.

title: The Ensign reprints the King Follett Sermon in two parts
speaker: Joseph Smith, reprinted by the Ensign
office: President of the Church (d. 1844); text reprinted under the Ensign's “Classics in Mormon Thought” series
venue: “The King Follett Sermon,” Ensign, April 1971, 13–14, and Ensign, May 1971, 13

witnesses.scribe: Ensign, May 1971 — part two
witnesses.note: The concluding installment, carrying its own headnote and the intelligence/eternalism material.

quotes.excerpt: The King Follett Sermon, one of the classics of Church literature, was given by the Prophet Joseph Smith at the April 7, 1844, conference of the Church in Nauvoo, Illinois. Some twenty thousand Saints were assembled. … Longhand notes of the discourse were made by Willard Richards, Wilford Woodruff, Thomas Bullock, and William Clayton. This reprint was taken from the Documentary History of the Church, vol. 6, pages 302–17. That volume notes: “This was not a stenographic report, but a carefully and skillfully prepared one made by these men who were trained in reporting and taking notes. Evidently, there are some imperfections in the report and some thoughts expressed by the Prophet which were not fully rounded out and made complete. …”
quotes.note: The whole editorial apparatus the Ensign supplies, and the reason this entry is worth having as its own row: the Church, in 1971, names the discourse “one of the classics of Church literature,” prints it under a standing series heading “Classics in Mormon Thought,” and does so with no doctrinal hedge whatsoever. The only caution offered is textual — the DHC's own admission that the report is imperfect — and even that is quoted from the source rather than issued by the Ensign in its own voice. The headnote does name all four longhand reporters, which is more transparency than most reprints of the sermon give. What it does not say is that the DHC text is an editorial amalgam of those four accounts rather than any one of them.

quotes.excerpt: God himself was once as we are now, and is an exalted man, and sits enthroned in yonder heavens! That is the great secret.
quotes.note: Both halves of the Father-status axis in one sentence, printed under the section heading “God an Exalted Man”: past mortality (“was once as we are now”) and attainment (“is an exalted man”). Per the precedent set on kfd-1844-q1, that pairing takes both tags. Hearsay downgraded to C for this quote: these are not the words of any of the four contemporaneous witnesses but the smoothed 1855 History draft reading, which is exactly the amalgam kfd-1844 flags in its own notes.

quotes.excerpt: In order to understand the subject of the dead, for consolation of those who mourn for the loss of their friends, it is necessary we should understand the character and being of God and how He came to be so; for I am going to tell you how God came to be God. We have imagined and supposed that God was God from all eternity. I will refute that idea, and take away the veil, so that you may see. … It is the first principle of the gospel to know for a certainty the character of God, and to know that we may converse with Him as one man converses with another, and that He was once a man like us; yea, that God himself, the Father of us all, dwelt on an earth, the same as Jesus Christ Himself did
quotes.note: Denial — FATHER-ALWAYS-GOD is carried here for the explicit rejection, “We have imagined and supposed that God was God from all eternity. I will refute that idea.” Set this beside lectures-on-faith-decanonized-1921-q3, which is the proposition being refuted, printed in the Church's own canon until 1921 and here refuted in the Church's own magazine in 1971. Hearsay C: same amalgam problem as q2, and note that Bullock at this point actually reads “he was God from the begin of all Eternity,” which is the opposite of what the smoothed text says — see kfd-1844.

quotes.excerpt: and you have got to learn how to be gods yourselves, and to be kings and priests to God, the same as all gods have done before you, namely, by going from one small degree to another, and from a small capacity to a great one; from grace to grace, from exaltation to exaltation, until you attain to the resurrection of the dead, and are able to dwell in everlasting burnings, and to sit in glory, as do those who sit enthroned in everlasting power.
quotes.note: The chain clause, and the single most important thing to know about this entry is that the Ensign prints it in the smoothed form. “The same as all gods have done before you” is the amalgam. Of the four contemporaneous accounts only Clayton attests a comparison class of Gods (“as all Gods has done”); Bullock has the weaker “same as all have done” with no “Gods” at all; Richards and Woodruff record the deification injunction with no comparison clause attached to it. So the reading that reaches 1971 readers — and, through them, most later citation of the sermon — rests on one witness and silently resolves a real divergence. See kfd-1844-q2, where the divergence is laid out. Hearsay C. Referent “father” for consistency with kfd-1844-q2, though strictly the clause is about the class of gods rather than the Father as such.

quotes.excerpt: The mind or the intelligence which man possesses is co-equal [co-eternal] with God himself. … God never had the power to create the spirit of man at all. God himself could not create himself. Intelligence is eternal and exists upon a self-existent principle. It is a spirit from age to age and there is no creation about it.
quotes.note: From the May installment. Organization over begetting, in the Church's own current magazine archive, in direct tension with fp-1909 and with the viviparous statements of the mid-century — which is worth noting given that all of it remains hosted side by side today. The bracket is the apparatus datum: “co-equal [co-eternal]” is an editorial gloss carried over from the Documentary History, and the same silent-correction convention appears throughout the reprint (“I will call [for] the attention,” “I calculate [intend] to edify you”). The Ensign supplies no footnotes of its own and no marginal apparatus; the brackets are the only editorial marks in the text. Hearsay C.

quotes.excerpt: This is the conclusion of the King Follett Sermon, delivered by the Prophet Joseph Smith at the April 7, 1844, conference of the Church in Nauvoo, Illinois. The first part of this classic was reprinted in the April Ensign (page 12). Readers should be reminded that the account of the talk was reconstructed from longhand notes taken by four brethren. It is also important to know that the Prophet's enemies were within just a few months of bringing about his death. This reprint was taken from the Documentary History of the Church, volume 6, pages 302–17.
quotes.note: The May headnote. “Reconstructed from longhand notes taken by four brethren” is a franker description of the text's status than the April headnote gave, and it is the closest the Church came in 1971 to saying that no single witness underwrites the printed wording. Small apparatus discrepancy worth recording: this headnote places the first installment at page 12, while the citation line on the April article reads “Ensign, Apr. 1971, 13–14.”

notes: Both installments were read verbatim from the live churchofjesuschrist.org pages on 2026-08-10; the quotations above are the hosted text exactly, including its bracketed editorial insertions and its section headings (“God an Exalted Man,” “Eternal Life to Know God and Jesus Christ,” “The Immortal Intelligence”). Filed as a citation of kfd-1844 rather than as an original, because the value of the entry is the event, not the text: in April and May 1971 — at the high-water mark of Correlation, in the first months of the newly consolidated Ensign, under a First Presidency headed by Joseph Fielding Smith — the Church reprinted the most theologically radical sermon in its history, in full, over two issues, framed admiringly and without a single doctrinal caveat. The same May 1971 issue carries Smith's own First Presidency message denying that God progresses in knowledge or power (jfs-progression-1971). Those two texts are thirteen pages and one issue apart, which is as concise a demonstration as the dataset contains that the C question and the D question are independent: the Church President could print “God himself was once as we are now” and “his progression consists not in gaining more knowledge or power” in the same magazine without contradiction, because they are not the same claim. Correlation graded current-correlated: both installments remain hosted in the official Gospel Library archive today and are reachable from the Church's own search. Textual caution repeated from kfd-1844 and applied per quote via hearsayByQuote: the reprint is the Documentary History text, an editorial amalgam of the Richards, Woodruff, Bullock, and Clayton accounts, and it is not identical with any of them. Where the amalgam and the witnesses diverge — most consequentially at “the same as all gods have done before you” — the quote notes say so. Do not treat any wording in this entry as a fifth witness to what was said on 7 April 1844.

title: Joseph Fielding Smith “restates for the Church and for the world” — and the Father “knows all things”
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith
office: President of the Church
venue: General conference, Saturday morning session

quotes.excerpt: Since the Lord has revealed his everlasting gospel anew to us in this day and has made The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints the custodian and dispenser of its saving truths, I desire now to restate for the Church and for the world a few of those eternal principles which must be accepted by mankind if they will save themselves.
quotes.note: The framing is the reason this entry exists. What follows is not an incidental remark but a Church President's deliberate, enumerated statement of the eternal principles, delivered in the opening address of his last April conference. Whatever the list contains and whatever it omits are both editorial decisions at the highest level.

quotes.excerpt: We know that our Heavenly Father is a glorified, exalted personage who has all power, all might, and all dominion, and that he knows all things. We testify that he, through his Only Begotten Son, is the Creator of this earth and of worlds without number, all of which are peopled by his spirit children.
quotes.note: Denial, and marked implied because Smith does not name the divine-progression debate here — he simply asserts the omniscience that settles it. Read with jfs-progression-1971 one month later, where the same man says the thing outright (“not in gaining more knowledge or power”); this conference address is that ruling in its doctrinal-summary form. Deliberately not tagged FATHER-BECAME-GOD: “glorified, exalted personage” is adjectival diction describing a state, not an assertion that he attained it, and tagging attainment off a participle would be retrojection — though the observation belongs on the record, since Smith elsewhere affirmed the couplet. The worlds-without-number clause is a plurality of creations under one God, not a succession of Gods, hence MANY-WORLDS and not INFINITE-CHAIN.

quotes.excerpt: We testify that he is infinite and eternal and that he ordained the laws whereby his spirit children might have power to advance and progress and become like him.
quotes.note: Carried as the negative datum. This is the entire forward-direction content of a formal restatement of eternal principles by a Church President: likeness, not increase. No eternal increase, no continuation of the seeds, no spirit offspring of our own, no Mother — and the sentence's other half places infinitude and eternity on the Father's side of the ledger while progress stays on ours. Theosis alone carries no forward tag.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/1971/1971-04-smith-out-of-the-darkness.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; all three excerpts were independently re-fetched from that live page during drafting on 2026-08-10 and returned verbatim. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. 1971 is the first year of the modern hosted archive, which is why this address can be graded current-correlated at all — the same material a year earlier would sit in a Conference Report. The entry's value is twofold: an omniscience assertion in the highest-authority register available, and an omission, since the enumerated eternal principles contain nothing of the generative or backward axes. Read against jfs-progression-1971, jfsmith-doctrines-salvation-1954 (where “our Father had a Father and so on” sits one page after “How God Does Not Progress”), and jfs-ignoramuses-1914.

title: Joseph Fielding Smith: progression “not in gaining more knowledge or power”
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith
office: President of the Church
venue: First Presidency message, “The Most Important Knowledge,” Ensign, May 1971

quotes.excerpt: And I am grateful that we know he is an infinite and eternal being who knows all things and has all power and whose progression consists not in gaining more knowledge or power, not in further perfecting his godly attributes, but in the increase and multiplying of his kingdoms.
quotes.note: Denial — the definitive official statement of the only-in-dominions position, from a sitting Church President in a First Presidency message. Note the mechanism: God's progression is relocated into the expansion of kingdoms, i.e. the forward/generative chain.

notes: Smith had argued this position for decades in Doctrines of Salvation (which prints “HOW GOD DOES NOT PROGRESS” roughly a page before “The Prophet taught that our Father had a Father and so on” — denying progression while affirming the regress, proof the two questions are independent). This 1971 First Presidency message is the position's most official form.

title: Theodore M. Burton: exaltation defined as “that possibility of an eternal family relationship”
speaker: Theodore M. Burton
office: Assistant to the Council of the Twelve
venue: General conference, Saturday afternoon session

quotes.excerpt: That possibility of an eternal family relationship is what is meant by exaltation and eternal life. This eternal preservation of my family relationship can be my inheritance in God's kingdom if I will pay the price to achieve it. Even those in the celestial kingdom who have not paid the full price of obedience to attain such further exaltation will have immortality only and not eternal life within God's family organization.
quotes.note: A definition, not an allusion — “is what is meant by.” The whole address is built to answer what exaltation is, and the answer is preservation of the family one already has. Note the verbs: preservation, inheritance, not increase or enlargement.

quotes.excerpt: Thus, full salvation in its true and full meaning is synonymous with exaltation and eternal life. This inheritance within the actual family of God the Eternal Father, through Jesus Christ, is the burden of the scriptures and should be the goal of every man, woman, and child born upon this earth. This full salvation is obtained only in and through the family unit preserved throughout eternity.
quotes.note: The definition restated and totalized: full salvation is “obtained only in and through the family unit preserved throughout eternity.” The direction of belonging runs upward — an inheritance within God's family — rather than outward into a family of one's own.

quotes.excerpt: Unless, then, through obedience to the laws of God you can qualify yourself to go to the temple and have your family sealed to you, you will live forever separately and singly in an unmarried state. It seems to me that would be a very lonesome type of existence—to live without the warming influence of family life among those you love, who in turn love you.
quotes.note: The reframe, and it is a clean one. Burton takes D&C 132:17's penalty and cashes it out as loneliness. What the verse says the unexalted lose is enlargement and godhood; what Burton says they lose is company. Compare morris-eternal-increase-1959, where the same verse is glossed as being “stripped of the greatest power, that of eternal increase,” thirteen years earlier.

quotes.excerpt: Therefore, when they are out of the world they neither marry nor are given in marriage; but are appointed angels in heaven, which angels are ministering servants, to minister for those who are worthy of a far more, and an exceeding, and an eternal weight of glory. For these angels did not abide in my law; therefore, they cannot be enlarged, but remain separately and singly, without exaltation, in their saved condition, to all eternity; and from henceforth are not gods, but are angels of God forever and ever.
quotes.note: D&C 132:16–17 read from the pulpit with no gloss of any kind — Burton introduces it and moves straight on to Elijah. Graded affirms because the increase claim is on the page in the verse's own words (“cannot be enlarged … are not gods”), stated as what the unexalted lack; the affirmation is the scripture's, not the speaker's, and the surrounding gloss in q3 has already redescribed the loss as loneliness. This is the pattern the dataset should watch for in the 1970s: the increase text stays in the pulpit while the increase reading leaves it.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/1972/1972-04-burton-salvation-and-exaltation.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; all four excerpts were independently re-fetched from that live page during drafting on 2026-08-10 and returned verbatim. Two typographic normalizations, no words changed: the vault and the hosted page render apostrophes as curly quotes, rendered straight here, and the hosted page carries the scripture reference parentheticals that follow q4, which are omitted. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. Filed sourceType original with a citesId edge to dc-132, because the address is Burton's own definitional argument and the revelation is evidence inside it rather than the entry's whole value. The talk is worth reading whole for the dataset's purposes: it is an entire conference address on what exaltation means, delivered by a general authority, in which the word children appears only as mortal posterity and the words increase, seed, and spirit children never appear outside the scripture block.

title: Marion G. Romney: “God is the father of man's spirit, even as his earthly father is the father of his mortal body”
speaker: Marion G. Romney
office: Second Counselor in the First Presidency
venue: General conference, Sunday morning session, Salt Lake City

quotes.excerpt: This is so because they know that it is the universal law of nature in the plant, animal, and human worlds for reproducing offspring to reach in final maturity the likeness of their parents. They reason that the same law is in force with respect to the offspring of God. Their objective is, therefore, to someday be like their heavenly parents.
quotes.note: The argument from natural law, restated from the First Presidency nine years after romney-1964 made it in the Twelve. It is tagged only for the plural: “their heavenly parents” is a Heavenly Mother claim on the same standard as proclamation-1995 and renlund-2020, dropped without comment into the premise of a different argument. The reproduction argument itself is left untagged exactly as romney-1964-q1 was — every clause is about offspring growing into the likeness of parents, and the generative reading is supplied by the reader. Note what is missing relative to 1964: there, “this process” was said to be “infinitely repeated in nature” and God himself was placed inside it; here the law is stated and the Father is not put under it. The backward half has been dropped.

quotes.excerpt: “Begotten sons and daughters unto God.” Can this be true in light of the fact that we all know that we are begotten sons and daughters of our earthly fathers? Yes, it is true because human souls are dual beings—spirits tabernacled in bodies of flesh and bone. The revelation says, “… the spirit and the body are the soul of man.” (D&C 88:15.) God is the father of man’s spirit, even as his earthly father is the father of his mortal body.
quotes.note: Affirmation, and the cleanest statement of the mechanism from a member of the First Presidency in the modern corpus. Romney raises the obvious objection himself — we already know who begot us — and answers it not by softening “begotten” but by dividing the object: two fathers, two begettings, one for the spirit and one for the body, on the same verb. That exact parallel is what earns the viviparous tag rather than the mechanism-unstated reading applied at kimball-intelligence-spirit-form-1978; nothing is said about gestation, but the analogy is to physical fatherhood and is offered as an explanation rather than an image. D&C 76:22–24 is quoted unglossed apart from this, and no Mother appears in the sentence — the begetting is the Father's alone here, which is a persistent asymmetry in the corpus and not peculiar to Romney.

quotes.excerpt: He thinks of himself, as the scriptures teach, possessed of the innate ability, as are all other reproducing offspring, to reach in final maturity the status of his heavenly parents and have “glory added upon [his] head for ever and ever.”
quotes.note: The nature argument's conclusion, and the strongest form it takes in the address: not merely likeness but “the status of his heavenly parents,” reached “in final maturity” by the same law that governs “all other reproducing offspring.” Tagged for the plural again. Deliberately not tagged forward — status is theosis, and per the A-is-not-B rule reaching the parents' status does not by itself assert that the exalted beget. The clause Romney appends from Abraham 3:26 is doing the work the older sources would have done with “continuation of the seeds.” Square brackets are the published text's.

quotes.excerpt: The truth is, my beloved brethren and sisters, man is a child of God—a God in embryo.
quotes.note: Untagged: theosis, and the phrase is inherited rather than coined — richards-gods-in-embryo-1914 and hunter-gods-in-embryo-1945 use it in the same sense, and in all three the embryo metaphor does its work on the human side of the ledger. Kept because it is the sentence the address builds to, and because it shows the vocabulary of literal generation surviving into 1973 as a figure of speech in the very talk that also states the mechanism literally at q2.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/1973/1973-04-romney-mana-child-of-god.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; all four excerpts were independently re-fetched from the live page during drafting and returned verbatim. Two things make this the most substantial modern statement of literal spirit parentage in the corpus. It is addressed explicitly to non-members as well as members (“wherever you are”) and offered as the remedy for a “sick and dying society,” so the doctrine is being advertised rather than protected. And it is spoken by a counselor in the First Presidency in 1973 — after mcconkie-family-affair-1970 had already begun substituting the family-unit vocabulary, and five years before kimball-intelligence-spirit-form-1978 would describe the same premortal transition as intelligences being given “spirit form.” Read alongside romney-1964 and romney-mother-in-heaven-1948, where the same man said of the process, “I do not know the process.”

title: Eldred G. Smith: “the same type of experiences they had done”
speaker: Eldred G. Smith
office: Patriarch to the Church
venue: General conference, Saturday afternoon session

quotes.excerpt: In the heavens, before the earth was formed, the plan of this earth life was explained to all of us. We were then but spirit offspring of our Father and Mother in heaven.
quotes.note: The opening sentence of the talk. “Spirit offspring of our Father and Mother in heaven” asserts the Mother and premortal parentage; no mechanism is named, so HEAVENLY-MOTHER alone and no spirit-birth tag.

quotes.excerpt: We all learned then that through this earth life experience we would have the opportunity of going through the same type of experiences they had done and so become as they are.
quotes.note: The sentence that makes this an original rather than another Heavenly Mother mention. “They” is the Father and Mother of the preceding sentence, and what is predicated of them is a completed earth life: mortality is not merely our probation, it is a repetition of theirs. That is FATHER-MORTAL-EXPERIENCE, stated obliquely but unmistakably, and delivered in a currently hosted general conference talk. Per the Father-status precedent it takes that tag alone — “become as they are” is what we may attain, and nothing is said here about how the Father attained anything, so no FATHER-BECAME-GOD. The Mother is swept into the same claim, which is rarer still: whatever the Father did, she did. Referent father for the tagged clause even though the pronoun is plural, since the category concerns the Father's status.

quotes.excerpt: The records tell us that we all shouted for joy at this glorious news.
quotes.note: The next sentence, kept so the reader can see there is no retreat, qualification, or scriptural hedge attached — the King Follett claim is stated in two clauses and the talk moves straight on to Adam and Eve. The remainder of the address is about opposition and agency and never returns to the point.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/1973/1973-10-smith-opposition-in-order-to-strengthen-us.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; the two categorized excerpts were additionally re-fetched from that live page during drafting and returned verbatim. It also matters that this survives on the Church's own site: the claim is not quarantined in a 19th-century sermon but sits in the searchable modern archive.

title: Spencer W. Kimball reads “a continuation of the seeds forever and ever” into the conference record
speaker: Spencer W. Kimball
office: President of the Council of the Twelve
venue: General conference, Sunday afternoon session

quotes.excerpt: They are they who are priests and kings, who have received of his fulness, and of his glory; And are priests of the Most High, after the order of Melchizedek, which was after the order of Enoch, which was after the order of the Only Begotten Son. Wherefore, as it is written, they are gods, even the sons of God—
quotes.note: D&C 76:56–58 read verbatim with no gloss. Uncategorized on the dataset's standing rule that bare theosis — “they are gods, even the sons of God” — is not by itself evidence for the generative or backward axes; it is carried because what Kimball chose to read aloud is the datum.

quotes.excerpt: … and they shall pass by the angels, and the gods which are set there, to their exaltation and glory in all things, as hath been sealed upon their heads, which glory shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever. Then shall they be gods, because they have no end … then shall they be gods, because they have all power, and the angels are subject unto them … … if ye receive me in the world, then shall ye know me, and shall receive your exaltation; that where I am ye shall be also.
quotes.note: D&C 132:19, 20, 23, introduced only as “the blessings of eternity” and read without comment. Affirms, because the increase language is present in the verse's own terms — continuation of the seeds — but the affirmation is the revelation's; Kimball adds nothing, and the ellipses are his own, printed in the text. The elisions are the ones he made: verse 20's middle clauses and the jump to verse 23. Compare hunter-beget-spirit-children-1949, where the same verse is read and then glossed as “the power to beget spirit children,” and renlund-2020, where it is read again with the gloss long gone.

title: Marion G. Romney reads Whitney's “Elias” from the pulpit: “In solemn council sat the Gods”
speaker: Marion G. Romney
office: Second Counselor in the First Presidency
venue: General conference, Saturday morning session

quotes.excerpt: In the following lines from his “Elias: An Epic of the Ages,” the late Elder Orson F. Whitney paraphrased what Abraham and other seers have revealed concerning the proceedings and consequences of that heavenly council and the role Jesus played in it. Now listen to these majestic lines of Brother Whitney:
quotes.note: The warrant, and the reason the entry exists: a counselor in the First Presidency introduces a poem as a paraphrase of revelation — not as illustration, not as devotional verse — and then reads roughly a hundred and sixty lines of it into the conference record. The classification is the datum, the same move McConkie makes for the hymn in mcconkie-family-affair-1970.

quotes.excerpt: In solemn council sat the Gods, … That awful hour was one When thought doth most avail; Of worlds unborn the destiny Hung trembling in the scale.
quotes.note: Deliberately uncategorized, and this is the entry's point. A council of plural Gods is a plurality, not a succession, and INFINITE-CHAIN requires succession-of-Gods language; nothing here says any of these Gods stands above or before another, or that the Father has a Father. This is exactly the text a careless reading would file under divine regress, and it is the dataset's job not to. Verse line breaks rendered as running text; the ellipsis is Romney's own, printed in the text.

quotes.excerpt: ‘Go forth, thou Chosen of the Gods, Whose strength shall in thee dwell! … ‘By arm divine, both mine and thine, The lost thou shalt restore, And man, redeemed, with God shall be, As God forevermore.
quotes.note: The Father's decree in the poem, and its promise for man. Two things sit side by side that the taxonomy keeps apart: plural Gods addressed as a body (“thou Chosen of the Gods”) and theosis (“As God forevermore”). Neither carries a category — theosis is not evidence for generative exaltation, and the plural is not a chain. Verse line breaks rendered as running text; the internal ellipsis marks the intervening stanza.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/1973/1973-10-romney-jesus-christ-our-redeemer.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; all three excerpts were independently re-fetched from that live page during drafting on 2026-08-10 and returned verbatim, allowing for verse line breaks, which the hosted page sets as separate lines and which are rendered here as running text. This entry is filed for what it does not support as much as for what it does. It belongs in the corpus because a 1973 First Presidency address treats a plural-Gods council text as revealed truth in the highest-visibility setting the Church has, and it should never be cited for the backward axis, because the poem's Gods are contemporaries in one council, not a line of ancestors. Read against packer-parentage-1984, which eleven years later deflates plurality language to the Godhead.

title: H. Burke Peterson: an eternal mother, “a cocreator of spiritual offspring”
speaker: H. Burke Peterson
office: First Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric
venue: General conference, Friday afternoon session

quotes.excerpt: In her high duty and service to humanity, endowing with immortality eternal spirits, she is co-partner with the Creator himself.
quotes.note: David O. McKay, Gospel Ideals, quoted by Peterson. Carried as a conflation guard: “co-partner with the Creator” and “endowing with immortality eternal spirits” describe mortal childbearing — giving already-existing spirits bodies — not the begetting of new spirits, and the phrase should not be cited for generative exaltation. Peterson's own claim two pages later is a different and much stronger one.

quotes.excerpt: —A mother whose energy is so sapped that she is sometimes neglecting her call from the Lord, a call that will one day prepare her to become an eternal mother—a cocreator of spiritual offspring.
quotes.note: Explicit, and dropped without ceremony into the middle of a list of the costs of working outside the home. “Spiritual offspring” names new spirit children and “cocreator” names the woman's own generative role; nothing here is metaphor for sealing or for mortal motherhood, since the whole clause is about what she becomes “one day.” The em dash and the leading dash are the printed list formatting. Compare hunter-beget-spirit-children-1949 and doxey-eternal-marriage-1969; this is the same doctrine surviving into the correlated hosted archive, in a talk indexed under motherhood rather than under exaltation.

quotes.excerpt: Our Father in heaven wants you to be in your home to guide these spirits as no one else can, in spite of material sacrifices that may result. He created you to learn to be a good mother—an eternal mother. It is your first and foremost calling.
quotes.note: The same claim in its euphemistic register, and the pairing inside one address is the useful part: “eternal mother” alone states nothing about offspring, and if q2 were absent this sentence would read as ordinary sealing language. It is the second occurrence that shows what the first one meant.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/1974/1974-04-peterson-mother-catch-the-vision-of-your-call.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; all three excerpts were independently re-fetched from that live page during drafting on 2026-08-10 and returned verbatim. The parenthetical source citation following q1 is omitted. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. Speaker office matters for weighting: Peterson is a counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, not an apostle, and the address is a pastoral argument against mothers working outside the home rather than a doctrinal exposition — the strongest generative statement in the batch arrives as a subordinate clause inside that argument. That is itself the finding: in April 1974 the doctrine is available for casual use, needs no defense, and is stated to a general session of conference without qualification.

title: Bruce R. McConkie: a Father with “all truth,” who “lives in the family unit”
speaker: Bruce R. McConkie
office: Of the Council of the Twelve
venue: General conference, Saturday afternoon session, Salt Lake City

quotes.excerpt: True, a curtain has been drawn so we do not recall our associations there. But we do know that our Eternal Father has all power, all might, all dominion, and all truth and that he lives in the family unit. We do know that we are his children, created in his image, endowed with power and ability to become like him. We know he gave us our agency and ordained the laws by obedience to which we can obtain eternal life.
quotes.note: Denial on the progression axis, six years before the BYU fireside made it famous, and delivered in the softest possible packaging: “all truth” is item four in a list of things “we do know” about a premortal life we cannot remember, offered as reassurance rather than as correction. Set against mcconkie-heresies-1980 the continuity is exact and the tone could not be more different — no target, no heresy, no one being answered. FORWARD-EUPHEMISM for “he lives in the family unit,” the same formula given its fullest statement at mcconkie-family-affair-1970 and here compressed into a subordinate clause about God's own mode of existence. The closing clause is theosis and nothing more: “endowed with power and ability to become like him” names no offspring and no mechanism, and per the A-is-not-B rule it adds nothing to the forward tag beyond what the family-unit clause already carries.

quotes.excerpt: Truly he is more than the offspring of faithful fathers. He is in fact a son of God, a spirit offspring of the Almighty. He dwelt with the Eternal Father, saw his face, heard his voice, and what is more important than all else, he believed his word and kept his law.
quotes.note: Untagged on purpose. “A spirit offspring of the Almighty” is offspring language with the mechanism unstated — the same discipline applied at kimball-intelligence-spirit-form-1978 — and the subject is Spencer W. Kimball's premortal biography, not the origin of spirits in general. Kept because it shows what the doctrine is being used for in this address: divine parentage as the ground of foreordination, so that a Church president's qualifications begin before his birth.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/1974/1974-04-mcconkie-god-foreordains-his-prophets-and-his-people.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; the load-bearing sentence was independently re-fetched from the live page during drafting and returned verbatim. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. Filed as an original with a citesId edge to abraham-3, which McConkie quotes at length (Abr. 3:22–23) for the foreordination argument; the Jeremiah, Alma, Romans and Ephesians citations have no dataset entries. Context worth recording: this is the first general conference after Spencer W. Kimball became President, and the whole address is a case for the living prophet's authority. That the omniscience claim and the family-unit formula surface inside it, as unexamined premises of an argument about succession, is the datum — by 1974 the shape of God is settled enough to be used as scaffolding.

title: LeGrand Richards: the dead who never married, and “a continuation of the seeds forever and ever”
speaker: LeGrand Richards
office: Of the Council of the Twelve
venue: General conference, Saturday afternoon session

quotes.excerpt: Then he adds: “For they are the seed of the blessed of the Lord, and their offspring with them.” … That sounds like a continuation of the family, doesn't it?
quotes.note: Isaiah 65:23 turned to the millennial question, with Richards's own gloss attached as a rhetorical question. “A continuation of the family” is the euphemism in its softest form and the referent is the millennial earth, not the celestial kingdom; hedges. The elision removes the printed scripture reference.

quotes.excerpt: And the earth shall be given unto them for an inheritance; and they shall multiply and wax strong, (and they can't multiply unless they have that relationship of husband and wife) and their children shall grow up without sin unto salvation.
quotes.note: D&C 45:58 with Richards's own parenthetical interpolated into the verse — the printed text italicizes the parenthesis to mark it as his. Uncategorized, and carried as a conflation guard: the multiplying in view is millennial mortal childbearing, not post-mortal spirit offspring, and the interpolation argues only that marriage is a precondition of it. The move matters anyway, because it is the hinge of his argument that the unmarried dead must be given marriage.

quotes.excerpt: Then I think of the revelation concerning those who will inherit the celestial kingdom, and the Lord said: “… which glory shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever.”
quotes.note: D&C 132:19 quoted as the celestial promise, with no gloss beyond the framing clause; affirms, on the verse's own increase language. The ellipsis is Richards's, printed in the text. This is the load-bearing citation in an argument whose conclusion is that those who died young or unmarried must receive everything the married faithful receive.

quotes.excerpt: And so I expect some day to see the bride that my son has selected over there in the spirit world. If he can find one as noble as his little niece I have mentioned (my granddaughter), just think what a glorious day that will be.
quotes.note: The conclusion drawn in the first person and about his own dead son: courtship and marriage continue in the spirit world. Hedges — an apostle stating post-mortal marriage as expectation, immediately after the continuation-of-the-seeds verse, with the increase itself left implicit. Read against richards-eternal-increase-1945 (a different Richards) and eldred-smith-no-increase-1948 for the other side of the same argument.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/1974/1974-10-richards-what-after-death.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; all four excerpts were independently re-fetched from that live page during drafting on 2026-08-10 and returned verbatim. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. Filed sourceType original with a citesId edge to dc-132: the argument is Richards's own, built from his family's losses, and the revelation is one step in it. The pastoral occasion is the point of the entry. This is not a doctrinal exposition of eternal increase but a consolation address, and the increase texts are load-bearing in it — which is a better index of how settled the teaching was in October 1974 than any exposition would be, because nobody consoles a congregation with a contested doctrine.

title: Spencer W. Kimball: “I suppose 225,000 of you may become gods”
speaker: Spencer W. Kimball
office: President of the Church
venue: General conference, priesthood session

quotes.excerpt: And that reminds us of the 132nd section where he promises that those who have received this new and everlasting covenant and who live up to the covenants President Romney has been talking about will exceed the angels. He goes beyond the gods and angels that are waiting there to guard the gates.
quotes.note: D&C 132:19 in paraphrase rather than quotation, tied to the new and everlasting covenant. Hedges: the covenant condition and the passing-by-the-angels image are both here, the continuation of the seeds is not.

quotes.excerpt: Brethren, 225,000 of you are here tonight. I suppose 225,000 of you may become gods. There seems to be plenty of space out there in the universe. And the Lord has proved that he knows how to do it. I think he could make, or probably have us help make, worlds for all of us, for every one of us 225,000.
quotes.note: A Church President tells a counted congregation that all of them may become gods with worlds apiece. MANY-WORLDS is the tag the plural creations earn; the godhood claim itself is theosis and carries no forward tag on its own, and Kimball is careful in a way the dataset should record — the worlds are made for us, or with our help, and nothing is said about who peoples them. The arithmetic is not rhetorical flourish; he has just counted the room, and he repeats the number three times.

quotes.excerpt: Just think of the possibilities, the potential. Every little boy that has just been born becomes an heir to this glorious, glorious program. When he is grown, he meets a lovely woman; they are married in the holy temple. They live all the commandments of the Lord. They keep themselves clean. And then they become sons of God, and they go forward with their great program—they go beyond the angels, beyond the angels and the gods that are waiting there. They go to their exaltation.
quotes.note: The paragraph immediately following, and it supplies the condition the worlds paragraph left out: temple marriage. Hedges, on the eldred-smith-slavery-godhood-1950 precedent — godhood conditioned on celestial marriage, with the generative content unstated. Note what is absent from a priesthood-session sermon on becoming gods: no spirit children, no eternal increase, no Mother.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/1975/1975-10-kimball-the-privilege-of-holding-the-priesthood.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; all three excerpts were independently re-fetched from that live page during drafting on 2026-08-10 and returned verbatim. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. Filed sourceType original with a citesId edge to dc-132 for the paraphrase in q1. Register is the finding here. This is the plainest plural-godhood statement by a sitting Church President in the hosted modern archive, it is delivered offhand and with humour to a priesthood session, it survives on the Church's own site, and it says nothing whatever about spirit offspring — which is the shape the doctrine has taken by 1975: the destination is still openly taught, the mechanism has gone quiet. Read against kimball-godhood-1952 twenty-three years earlier, where the same man names eternal increase outright, and against kimball-1976 a year later, where he draws a boundary around a different speculative teaching.

title: Marion G. Romney: we inherit “the status of our heavenly parents” as we inherit our mortal parents'
speaker: Marion G. Romney
office: Second Counselor in the First Presidency
venue: General conference, Tuesday morning session

quotes.excerpt: This opened the way for an explanation that God himself is a soul, composed of a body of flesh and bones as tangible as man's, and a spirit; that he is a resurrected, glorified, exalted, omniscient, omnipotent, and—in spirit, and power, and influence—an omnipresent person, the ruler of the heavens and the earth and all things therein; that the spirits of all men are literally his “begotten sons and daughters.”
quotes.note: Two things at once. “Literally his begotten sons and daughters” is D&C 76:24 with the word literally added by Romney, which is the viviparous claim in its standard mid-century form; affirms. The attribute list denies divine progression by asserting omniscience and omnipotence, though Romney never names the debate, so that tag is graded on the assertion rather than on an argument. Two observations that stay out of the categories per the no-retrojection rule: “exalted” is a participle describing a state, not an assertion that he attained it, and “resurrected” logically entails a prior death and so a prior mortality — an entailment Romney does not draw and the dataset should not tag for him.

quotes.excerpt: As to why we are here on earth, I reminded him of the self-evident fact that, as the offspring of God, we inherit the capability of reaching, in full maturity, the status of our heavenly parents just as we inherit from our mortal parents the capability to attain to their mortal status; and that since God has a body of flesh and bones, it was necessary and perfectly natural for us, his spirit offspring, to obtain such bodies in order that we might be like him; that coming to earth was the means provided for us to obtain these bodies.
quotes.note: The inheritance argument stated as a self-evident fact: divine offspring reach the parental status the way children reach adulthood. Heavenly Mother affirmed the usual indirect way, by the plural “heavenly parents.” The forward tag is graded hedges deliberately — “the status of our heavenly parents” is parental-status language and the biological analogy is explicit, but Romney never says the mature offspring have offspring of their own, and reading increase into “status” would be exactly the symmetry inference the taxonomy keeps out of the categories.

quotes.excerpt: I know that we are human souls—composed of spirits begotten of God, tabernacled in mortal bodies of flesh and blood and bones.
quotes.note: The same claim moved into the closing testimony — “I know” rather than “I explained.” Carried because the register change is the datum: begotten spirits are not presented as speculation in April 1976 but as something a member of the First Presidency testifies to.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/1976/1976-04-romney-the-way-of-life.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; all three excerpts were independently re-fetched from that live page during drafting on 2026-08-10 and returned verbatim. The printed scripture-reference parenthetical following the D&C 76:24 quotation in q1 is omitted; no words changed. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. Entry referent is father — every backward-facing clause here is explicitly about God the Father, reached through the “offspring of God” framing of Acts 17. The frame deserves recording: the whole address is Romney's account of what he told a religionless stranger on an airplane, so the doctrine is presented as the missionary-level answer to where we came from, not as advanced material. Read against romney-mother-in-heaven-1948 (“I do not know the process”) and romney-1964; twenty-eight years after declining to describe the process, he is stating the parentage as self-evident.

title: Bruce R. McConkie: “the spirit children of an exalted, glorified Being, a Holy Man”
speaker: Bruce R. McConkie
office: Of the Council of the Twelve
venue: General conference, Sunday afternoon session

quotes.excerpt: We know, because the Lord has revealed it in this our day, that we are the spirit children of an exalted, glorified Being, a Holy Man who has a body of flesh and bones and who is our Father in heaven.
quotes.note: Hedges: spirit parentage of an embodied Father is asserted flatly, with no mechanism — no begetting, no birth, no Mother. “Holy Man” is the Moses 6:57 title Man of Holiness, not a claim about mortality, and “exalted, glorified” is adjectival and is not tagged as attainment; both observations stay in the note rather than in the categories. The framing “because the Lord has revealed it in this our day” is the certainty marker worth keeping: no hedge, no speculation label.

quotes.excerpt: We know that the name of the kind of life He lives is eternal life and that it consists of living in the family unit and of possessing all power, all might, and all dominion.
quotes.note: The McConkie vocabulary in one sentence. Eternal life defined as the family unit — hedges, the same euphemism he had already installed in mcconkie-family-affair-1970 (“eternal family units patterned after his eternal family”) — and “all power, all might, and all dominion” denying progression in knowledge or power. Marked implied because he does not name the divine-progression question here; the denial is precise and is his known position, which allowed increase in dominions while refusing it in power (mcconkie-mormon-doctrine). Note that the sentence describes the Father's life, so the family-unit euphemism is running backward as well as forward, but nothing is claimed about his origin and no backward tag is warranted.

quotes.excerpt: We know that He ordained and established the plan of salvation to enable us to advance and progress from our spirit state, to the same state of glory, honor, and exaltation which He Himself possesses.
quotes.note: The same-state claim, uncategorized because it is theosis: we advance to the state He possesses, which says nothing about how He came to possess it or about what we generate once there. Carried because it completes the three-sentence catechism McConkie opens the address with, and because “the same state … which He Himself possesses” is as close as the correlated 1970s pulpit comes to the couplet without quoting it.

quotes.excerpt: “In the resurrection, some are raised to be angels, others are raised to become Gods.” (Teachings, p. 312.)
quotes.note: Joseph Smith as quoted from Teachings of the Prophet Joseph Smith, read into the record without comment. Uncategorized — bare theosis — and given no citesId, because the dataset's Joseph Smith entries are specific sermons (kfd-1844, sermon-grove-1844, js-1842-discourse) and this Teachings page was not matched to one of them during drafting; an edge should not be invented to make the graph look connected.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/1976/1976-10-mcconkie-the-dead-who-die-in-the-lord.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; all four excerpts were independently re-fetched from that live page during drafting on 2026-08-10 and returned verbatim. The hosted page italicizes “eternal life” in q2 and the italics are dropped here; no words changed. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. Entry referent father: the Being described is named “our Father in heaven” in the same sentence. What makes this entry worth having is its economy — McConkie opens a funeral-themed conference address with a compressed catechism of origins, and in four sentences he asserts spirit parentage, defines eternal life as the family unit, forecloses progression in power, and promises the same state of exaltation, all without one word about spirit offspring, a Mother, or the Father's own beginning. Read against mcconkie-family-affair-1970 six years earlier and mcconkie-heresies-1980 four years later, where he polices this boundary explicitly.

title: Spencer W. Kimball: “authority to produce both spirit and body”
speaker: Spencer W. Kimball
office: President of the Church
venue: General conference, priesthood session

quotes.excerpt: We remember the numerous scriptures which, concentrated in a single line, were said by a former prophet, Lorenzo Snow: “As man is, God once was; and as God is, man may become.” This is a power available to us as we reach perfection and receive the experience and power to create, to organize, to control native elements.
quotes.note: The bare couplet, quoted by a sitting Church President in general conference and attributed to Snow by name — FATHER-MORTAL-EXPERIENCE only, per the standing precedent that the bare couplet claims past mortality and nothing more. What Kimball adds is not backward but forward: he immediately cashes the couplet out as creative power we will receive. Wording note: Kimball quotes the widely circulated variant, not Snow's published couplet. Snow's own form as carried in snow-couplet reads “As man now is, God once was: As God now is, man may be”; Kimball drops both “now”s, reads “man may become,” and adds an “and” at the caesura — the same drift already visible in talmage-af-1899.

quotes.excerpt: Millions of us have contributed toward the creation and the development of a spirit, but “the germ of this, God has placed within us. And when our spirits receive our bodies, and through our faithfulness we are worthy to be crowned, we will then receive authority to produce both spirit and body.
