office: Professor of Ancient Scripture, Brigham Young University
venue: Answers: Straightforward Answers to Tough Gospel Questions (Salt Lake City: Deseret Book, 1998), 168

witnesses.scribe: Alonzo L. Gaskill, The Savior, Symbols, and Salvation, ch. note 13
witnesses.note: Quotes the sentence with the page citation “Answers, 168,” in a note gathering statements that God became what He is by obedience to eternal law.

quotes.excerpt: God was once a man obtaining his exalted status by obedience to the laws of his own eternal Father.
quotes.note: One sentence carrying both halves at once: past mortality (“God was once a man”) and explicit divine parentage (“his own eternal Father”). Chain length is unstated and no chain is asserted, so no INFINITE-CHAIN tag — but the parentage is unhedged, which makes this one of the most recent flatly affirmative statements available from a named Latter-day Saint author.

notes: The book is not in the collated corpus; the sentence was verified verbatim against Gaskill's quotation, which supplies the page. The 1998-versus-2002 imprint question that trails this citation is now settled in favour of 1998: Gaskill's short-form note gives no year, but his own bibliography lists “McConkie, Joseph Fielding. 1998. Answers: Straightforward Answers to Tough Gospel Questions. Salt Lake City: Deseret Book,” and at least eight other independent bibliographies in the corpus (Harrell, Bradshaw, Gardner, Harris, Wilcox, Valletta, and two Dialogue articles) give the same 1998 Deseret Book imprint. No 2002 imprint appears anywhere in the corpus, so the entry is dated 1998. Never-official: a Deseret Book trade title in a question-and-answer format by a BYU religion professor, notable mainly for how plainly it states in 1998 what correlated materials had by then stopped saying.

title: Henry B. Eyring, “Do Not Delay”
speaker: Henry B. Eyring
office: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General Conference, October 1999, Salt Lake City

quotes.excerpt: It is the greatest of all the gifts of God. It is to live in families forever with our Heavenly Father and with Jesus Christ and to have eternal increase.
quotes.note: Defining eternal life. “Eternal increase” is the final term in the definition and receives no explanation; the surrounding argument is about not postponing repentance, so the phrase passes without the audience being asked to unpack it.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the live talk. The earliest item in this batch and a useful boundary marker: in 1999 an apostle can still put “eternal increase” in a definition of eternal life as though it needs no gloss, which is a different silence from the later one — assumed shared vocabulary rather than deliberate omission. Nothing in the talk distinguishes the two readings, and the entry does not claim to.

title: Sheri L. Dew, “Are We Not All Mothers?”
speaker: Sheri L. Dew
office: Second Counselor in the Relief Society General Presidency
venue: General Conference, October 2001, Salt Lake City

quotes.excerpt: For mother is the word that will define a righteous woman made perfect in the highest degree of the celestial kingdom, a woman who has qualified for eternal increase in posterity, wisdom, joy, and influence.
quotes.note: “Mother” is italicized in print. title: Bruce R. McConkie, Mormon Doctrine — “Eternal Progression,” “Spirit Children”
speaker: Bruce R. McConkie
office: Seventy, later Apostle
venue: Mormon Doctrine (Bookcraft)

quotes.excerpt: Spirit Children… 1. All men in pre-existence were the spirit children of God our Father, an exalted, glorified, and perfected Man. “The Father has a body of flesh and bones as tangible as man's” (D. & C. 130:22); the offspring born to him in that primeval sphere had bodies of spirit element… 2. In a future eternity, spirit children will be born to exalted, perfected, glorified couples for whom the family unit continues. The very glory of exalted beings is to have “a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever.” (D. & C. 132:19-25, 29-32; 131:1-4.) … Spirit Birth… 1. In the literal sense, the expression spirit birth has reference to the birth of the spirit in pre-existence. Spirits are actually born as the offspring of a Heavenly Father, a glorified and exalted Man. They will be born in a future eternity to future exalted beings for whom the family unit continues.
quotes.note: Two adjacent entries, “Spirit Children” and “Spirit Birth,” quoted together because the pair is the claim: the same begetting is predicated of the Father in the past and of exalted couples in the future, in the same words. The vocabulary is deliberately literalist — “in the literal sense,” “actually born,” “born to him,” “birth process” in the companion “Spirit Bodies” entry — which is what earns SPIRIT-BIRTH-VIVIPAROUS rather than the adoption tag; contrast Roberts, who reaches the same begetting while holding the intelligence uncreated (bh-roberts-tripartite). INFINITE-CHAIN rests on the forward half specifically — the glory of exalted beings is “a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever,” an unending continuation, not a single further generation — and on the fact that the past and future halves are stated as one repeating pattern rather than two unrelated facts. The Father is described as “an exalted, glorified, and perfected Man,” attainment language without a mortality claim, which per the Father-status precedent would be FATHER-BECAME-GOD; that reading is left to q2, where McConkie makes it explicit rather than adjectival. 2nd ed. (1966) pp. 523; 1st ed. (1958) pp. 678–679.

quotes.excerpt: “Every man who reigns in celestial glory is a god to his dominions,” the Prophet said. Hence, the Father, who shall continue to all eternity as the God of exalted beings, is a God of Gods. Further, as the Prophet also taught, there is “a God above the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. … If Jesus Christ was the Son of God, and John discovered that God the Father of Jesus Christ had a Father, you may suppose that he had a Father also. Where was there ever a son without a father? … Hence if Jesus had a Father, can we not believe that he had a Father also?” In this way both the Father and the Son, as also all exalted beings, are now or in due course will become Gods of Gods.
quotes.note: The “God of Gods” entry, 2nd ed. (1966) p. 230, printing the Sermon in the Grove regress approvingly — from the same author whose 1980 fireside denounced divine progression in knowledge. Affirming the backward chain while denying divine progression: the two questions are independent, demonstrated within one corpus. Pagination now checked in both editions: 2nd ed. p. 230, 1st ed. (1958) p. 296, wording unchanged between them.

quotes.excerpt: Those who gain exaltation, having thus enjoyed the fullness of eternal progression, become like God. It should be realized that God is not progressing in knowledge, truth, virtue, wisdom, or any of the attributes of godliness. He has already gained these things in their fullness. But he is progressing in the sense that his creations increase, his dominions expand, his spirit offspring multiply, and more kingdoms are added to his domains. (Doctrines of Salvation, vol. 1, pp. 5-10.)
quotes.note: The “Eternal Progression” entry, 2nd ed. p. 174 / 1st ed. p. 221. A denial, and the canonical statement of the dominions-not-knowledge move — the same distinction B. H. Roberts had used in 1911 to affirm divine progress (roberts-progress-of-god-1911), here run in reverse to deny it, sourced to Joseph Fielding Smith. Worth reading beside q2 on the same page-range logic: God has a Father and is a God of Gods, but does not learn. Also note the third clause of the concession — “his spirit offspring multiply” — which concedes ongoing generation by the Father in the present tense while denying progression, and so keeps the forward chain of q1 alive inside the denial. One textual difference between editions, non-substantive to the tag: the 1st edition adds “and that even for those who participate in eternal progression in its fullest sense there are limits to the doctrine,” dropped in the 2nd.

notes: Placeholder closed in v2. All three excerpts were read from the Gospel Scholar Archive copies of both printings and their printed folios recorded: Mormon Doctrine, 1st ed. (Salt Lake City: Bookcraft, 1958; title page and June 1958 preface confirmed in the scan) — “Eternal Progression” p. 221, “God of Gods” p. 296, “Spirit Birth”/“Spirit Children” pp. 678–679; 2nd ed. (© 1966 Deseret Book) — pp. 174, 230, 523. Wording is identical across the two editions for every clause quoted here apart from one dropped subordinate clause in “Eternal Progression,” noted on q3, so the previously flagged first-edition pagination gap is closed and the verification flag is cleared. The url now points at the archive page for “Spirit Children,” since that is where q1 lives; the Internet Archive lending copy (archive.org/details/mormondoctrine0000mcco) remains a second witness but is not page-anchored. Never official — it drew First Presidency concern on publication, and the 1865 rule that a member may not publish doctrine without prior approval of the First Presidency and the Twelve (see fp-repudiation-1865) is precisely what it ignored — yet massively influential on lay understanding for half a century, which is exactly why it needs to be in the dataset with its status labelled honestly. Bookcraft/Deseret Book let it go out of print in 2010; that discontinuation is itself a retreat data point, and the reason its correlation status is discontinued rather than never-official. A further passage the maintainer may want as a fourth quote: the “Eternity to Eternity” entry, 2nd ed. p. 175, which states that spirit children “will have gone on to exaltation, having spirit children of their own” and that exalted beings go on “multiplying their race without end” — the cleanest INFINITE-CHAIN statement in the book. It is left out here only because its first-edition location was not checked.

title: Neal A. Maxwell's “stunners”: worlds without number, and man in the beginning with God
speaker: Neal A. Maxwell
office: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, Sunday afternoon session

quotes.excerpt: Through multiple revelations and translations, for example, came a description of a universe far, far exceeding the astrophysics of the 1830s, a cosmos containing “worlds without number” and advising us further that the “inhabitants thereof are begotten sons and daughters [of] God” (Moses 1:33; D&C 76:24).
quotes.note: Plural worlds under one God, with their inhabitants declared His begotten offspring — the D&C 76:24 clause, which is the strongest single sentence in the canon on the reach of divine paternity, quoted here without gloss and used as evidence of Joseph Smith's prophetic range rather than as a theological claim. Nothing successive is asserted: the worlds are many, the Father is one, and no earlier Father appears anywhere in the address. The bracketed “[of]” is the published text's.

quotes.excerpt: Revelations likewise came about our longevity as God’s spirit children, since “man was also in the beginning with God”—a declaration accompanied by even further glimmers about man’s eternal nature (D&C 93:29). These enunciations with their profound implications are major—challenging, for instance, the teaching that man was created in an instant “out of nothing.”
quotes.note: Untagged after consideration, and the reason is the discipline the dataset runs on. Maxwell asserts two things in one sentence — that we are God's spirit children, and that man was in the beginning with God, uncreated, against creation ex nihilo — and does not reconcile them. That is the exact pair whose reconciliation is what SPIRIT-BIRTH-VIVIPAROUS and SPIRIT-BIRTH-ADOPTION disagree about, and he takes neither side; tagging either would be reading the answer into a text that only poses the question. Nor is TRIPARTITE-FRAMEWORK available: there is no staging here, no intelligence tier named and no transition described, only two-stage eternalism of the kind the category's own definition warns against retrojecting. What the passage is genuinely evidence for is that in 2003 the uncreated eternality of the individual was still being preached from the pulpit as a Restoration “stunner” — the metaphysical premise on which the whole regress question depends, stated by an Apostle without any of the regress being drawn from it.

quotes.excerpt: If Joseph Smith had been the conduit for only one such divine revelation, it would be, standing alone, sufficient to ensure his prophetic greatness. Yet even though God wants to give us “all that [He] hath,” we suffer from a poverty of perceptions! (D&C 84:38).
quotes.note: The D&C 84:38 formula, deployed exactly as renlund-divine-nature-2022-q6 deploys it — maximal in scope, empty of content. “All that He hath” is the inheritance vocabulary that carries the generative claim in current discourse without ever naming what is inherited, and here it is put to a rhetorical purpose that has nothing to do with posterity: it is a rebuke for small imagination. Hedges. The bracketed “[He]” is the published text's.

notes: Quoted verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/2003/2003-10-maxwell-how-choice-a-seer.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; the live page was re-fetched during drafting on 2026-08-10 and returned the byline (“Elder Neal A. Maxwell, Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles”) and the opening of both “stunner” paragraphs verbatim. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. A deliberately lean entry. The address names three Restoration “stunners” — a vast cosmos, the eternal pre-existence of man, and the reality of the resurrected Christ — and two of them touch this dataset's axes without landing on any of its claims. Its value is negative and precise: this is what a maximally expansive, deliberately provocative apostolic statement of Restoration metaphysics looks like in 2003, and it contains no chain of Gods, no Father of the Father, no eternal increase, and no Heavenly Mother. Compare maxwell-heavenly-mother-1978 by the same speaker twenty-five years earlier, where the Mother is the closing question of the address; here she is absent from a talk whose whole subject is what the Restoration revealed about the nature of God. The citesId edge is to moses-1 for the quotation of Moses 1:33.

It was from him that I learned that we might cultivate these affections, and grow and increase in the same to all eternity; while the result of our endless union would be an offspring as numerous as the stars of heaven, or the sands of the sea shore. …”
quotes.note: The explicit claim in this talk is quoted, not authored: an endless post-mortal union whose *result* is offspring beyond counting. Eyring reads it approvingly, without qualification, as the doctrine Joseph Smith taught Pratt about eternal families, and then moves straight to how priesthood service changes a man's feelings — no gloss on the offspring clause. The hearsay override (D) is for the quotation's own provenance, not Eyring's: Pratt is recollecting an 1840 conversation years afterward, and the Autobiography was published posthumously by his son.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the hosted talk on churchofjesuschrist.org. Eyring cites Autobiography of Parley P. Pratt, ed. Parley P. Pratt Jr. (1938), 259–60; that text has no dataset entry of its own, so no citesId edge is drawn — the two existing Parley P. Pratt entries are the 1853 heirship discourse and the 1855 Key to the Science of Theology. The pairing is the interesting part: Eyring's own sentence stays inside the euphemism register while the passage he reads aloud, three paragraphs later, states post-mortal procreation outright.

title: Keith B. McMullin: “an exalted man” and “the same unchangeable God” in one sentence
speaker: Keith B. McMullin
office: Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric
venue: General conference, Sunday morning session, October 2008 (Ensign, Nov. 2008)

quotes.excerpt: One of the overarching truths of the Restoration is that God lives and dwells in His heavens, that He is an exalted man with “a body of flesh and bones,” and that He is yesterday, today, and forever the same unchangeable God, the fountain of all virtue and truth.
quotes.note: Both directions in one sentence, joined by “and.” “He is an exalted man” is the predicate construction the Father-status precedent reads as attainment language — the same phrasing that made Milton R. Hunter's October 1948 address a false negative (hunter-exalted-man-1948-q1) — while the second clause, footnoted to D&C 20:17, asserts beginningless unchangeableness. Neither is developed: this is the talk's opening line, and the rest of the address is about welfare, prayer, and priesthood blessings. Two caveats against reading too much in. “Exalted man” here carries no mortality claim and no couplet, so FATHER-MORTAL-EXPERIENCE is not tagged; and “unchangeable” in D&C 20:17 is a constancy-of-character formula, so DIVINE-PROGRESSION is left off rather than retrojected onto it. What the quote does show is that in 2008 an officer of the Presiding Bishopric could still call the exalted-man premise an overarching truth of the Restoration, in general conference, without appearing to notice the tension he had just built.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the hosted talk on churchofjesuschrist.org, footnotes included (n. 1 is D&C 130:22; n. 2 is D&C 20:17). Referent is unambiguous: the subject is God the Father, who is distinguished from the Son throughout the address, and Christ is named separately as “the Firstborn of our Father's spirit children.” Stance flagged for review because the quote records opposite directions on the same axis within a single sentence — the FATHER-ALWAYS-GOD reading rests on the unchangeableness clause, the FATHER-BECAME-GOD reading on “exalted man,” and a reviewer may prefer to split them across two quotes.

title: Henry B. Eyring, “Adversity” — mortality as preparation for “the trust of an endless posterity”
speaker: Henry B. Eyring
office: First Counselor in the First Presidency
venue: General conference, Saturday morning session, April 2009 (Ensign, May 2009)

quotes.excerpt: God gave us the gift of living in mortality so that we could be prepared to receive the greatest of all the gifts of God, which is eternal life. Then our spirits will be changed. We will become able to want what God wants, to think as He thinks, and thus be prepared for the trust of an endless posterity to teach and to lead through tests to be raised up to qualify to live forever in eternal life.
quotes.note: The forward chain stated plainly, in a sermon that otherwise contains no exaltation vocabulary at all: the posterity is post-mortal and endless, it is ours, we teach and lead it, and it passes through tests in order to qualify for eternal life — precisely the office the Father is described as holding over us in the sentence before. Tagged explicit rather than euphemism because a role, not a blessing, is being described; the caveat is that Eyring never says the posterity is begotten, so the mechanism is absent even though the relationship is not. The following paragraph doubles down on “that trust” as the thing mortality is preparing us for.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the hosted talk on churchofjesuschrist.org. Register datum as much as content datum: the strongest forward-chain sentence in this batch appears mid-paragraph in a talk about suffering, from a member of the First Presidency, with no scriptural citation attached and no elaboration afterward.

title: Richard G. Scott: “intelligences tabernacled with spirits would receive a body”
speaker: Richard G. Scott
office: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, Sunday morning session (Easter morning)

quotes.excerpt: What eternal purpose would our Father’s plan of happiness have had except it be made alive through the infinite and eternal Atonement of His gloriously obedient Son? What eternal purpose would have come from the Creation of the earth, where intelligences tabernacled with spirits would receive a body, if death were the end of existence and none would be resurrected?
quotes.note: All three tiers and both transitions in a single subordinate clause: intelligences, already tabernacled with spirits, coming to earth to receive a body. Tagged TRIPARTITE-FRAMEWORK on the same ground as brown-intelligences-then-spirits-1969 — the staging is stated, not read in — but the register is what makes it worth an entry. This is a rhetorical question inside an Easter sermon about the Atonement; the three-stage anthropology is not the subject, it is the unexamined furniture of the sentence, which is a better measure of how settled the model was in 2010 than any address that argues for it. Note also what is absent: no heavenly parents, no begetting, and no account of how an intelligence comes to be tabernacled with a spirit, so no SPIRIT-BIRTH tag attaches in either direction.

quotes.excerpt: May each of us renew our determination to teach true principles within the sanctity of our homes. As we do that, we will provide the greatest opportunity for happiness for the spirits entrusted to our care. Use the Church as a righteous tool to strengthen the home, but recognize that as parents we have the fundamental responsibility and privilege to be guided by the Lord in the upbringing of the spirit children He has entrusted to our care.
quotes.note: Kept for the semantic control it provides on the same page. “The spirit children He has entrusted to our care” means mortal children — already-existing spirits given to earthly parents — which is the modern sense of the phrase and the exact inverse of the mid-century sense in hunter-beget-spirit-children-1949, where spirit children are what exalted couples will beget. Untagged: nothing here is a claim about eternal increase. Recorded because a phrase search for “spirit children” across the modern corpus returns mostly sentences like this one.

notes: Quoted verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/2010/2010-04-scott-he-lives-all-glory-to-his-name.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; the live page was re-fetched during drafting on 2026-08-10 and returned the byline (“Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles”) and the “intelligences tabernacled with spirits” clause verbatim. Official published text, so A, and currently hosted, so current-correlated. A lean entry by design: the address is about the Resurrection and makes exactly one axis-bearing move. Its value is as a late, casual, currently hosted witness that the intelligence → spirit → body staging survives in apostolic speech thirty-two years after kimball-intelligence-spirit-form-1978 stated it as catechesis — surviving, by 2010, as a dependent clause nobody stops to explain.

title: Gospel Principles, ch. 47, “Exaltation”
speaker: Church Curriculum Department
office: Correlated basic-doctrine manual
venue: Gospel Principles (2011 edition), chapter 47

quotes.excerpt: Exaltation is eternal life, the kind of life God lives. He lives in great glory. He is perfect. He possesses all knowledge and all wisdom. He is the Father of spirit children. He is a creator. We can become like our Heavenly Father. This is exaltation.
quotes.note: The premise, stated plainly: the life we are promised is defined as the life God lives, and one of the six named features of that life is that He is “the Father of spirit children.” Tagged implied because the forward generative claim is not made here — the paragraph asserts A (we can become like Him) alongside a definition that contains B, and stops.

quotes.excerpt: They will be united eternally with their righteous family members and will be able to have eternal increase.
quotes.note: Item 3 of the five numbered blessings of exaltation, four pages after the definition above. “Eternal increase” appears with no gloss; nothing on the page tells the reader that the increase consists of spirit children.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the live page (both the opening definition and the numbered blessings list). This is the careful construction in its purest form: term A is defined as including spirit-parenthood, term B (“eternal increase”) is named as a blessing, and the manual never writes the sentence that joins them. The syllogism is complete in the reader's hands and unclosed on the page — deniable in either direction, which is presumably the point of building it this way. Note that neither half is itself an explicit forward claim, so the entry is euphemism twice over rather than explicit once; the explicitness lives only in the inference.

title: Russell M. Nelson, “Covenants” — eternal increase as an Abrahamic entitlement
speaker: Russell M. Nelson
office: Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, Sunday afternoon session, October 2011 (Ensign, Nov. 2011)

quotes.excerpt: Abraham's posterity would be numerous, entitled to an eternal increase, and also entitled to bear the priesthood.
quotes.note: One bullet in a six-item list of the Abrahamic promises. Eternal increase is asserted as a covenant entitlement — something the covenant confers, not merely a hope — but Nelson never says what increases, and the item sits between numerous posterity and priesthood as though it belonged to the same order of blessing. Thinner than the calibration case (penrose-endless-increase-1911), which supplies the content the phrase is standing in for.

quotes.excerpt: Ultimately, in the holy temple, we may become joint heirs to the blessings of an eternal family, as once promised to Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and their posterity. Thus, celestial marriage is the covenant of exaltation.
quotes.note: The talk's closing move on the axis: the temple sealing is named “the covenant of exaltation,” and the content of exaltation is given as “the blessings of an eternal family.” Two paragraphs earlier Nelson has chained D&C 84 — receive the priesthood, receive Christ, receive the Father, and “those who receive the Father receive all that He has” — but that chain is left as theosis and is not connected to the increase language, so the two halves never meet.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the hosted talk on churchofjesuschrist.org, footnotes included. No citesId: Nelson's D&C 132:30–31 quotation is the Abrahamic-promise passage, not the 132:19–20, 63 material the dc-132 entry records, and his Brigham Young quotation is from a different chapter of the same manual the tpby-1997 entry covers — both edges would be misleading. Included as a comprehensive-drop-box entry: a future President of the Church using the phrase in its bare covenant-list form, seven years before his own presidency.

title: D. Todd Christofferson, “The Doctrine of Christ” — the mechanism by which a past teaching stops being doctrine
speaker: D. Todd Christofferson
office: Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, Sunday morning session, April 2012 (Ensign, May 2012)

quotes.excerpt: At the same time it should be remembered that not every statement made by a Church leader, past or present, necessarily constitutes doctrine. It is commonly understood in the Church that a statement made by one leader on a single occasion often represents a personal, though well-considered, opinion, not meant to be official or binding for the whole Church.
quotes.note: The general rule, stated by a member of the Twelve in general conference: past leaders' statements are not doctrine by default. No doctrine is named, so this reframes the category rather than any particular teaching — but it is the canonical modern statement of the mechanism by which nineteenth-century teaching on divine ancestry and progression gets bracketed, and it is the passage later material tends to cite for that purpose.

quotes.excerpt: “How shall the Church know when these adventurous expeditions of the brethren into these highly speculative principles and doctrines meet the requirements of the statutes that the announcers thereof have been ‘moved upon by the Holy Ghost’? The Church will know by the testimony of the Holy Ghost in the body of the members, whether the brethren in voicing their views are ‘moved upon by the Holy Ghost’; and in due time that knowledge will be made manifest”
quotes.note: J. Reuben Clark Jr., 1954, reprinted by Christofferson. Two provenance points matter. First, only the second sentence is read in the body of the talk; the “adventurous expeditions” question, and Clark's adjoining observation that this “has happened about matters of doctrine (usually of a highly speculative character) where subsequent Presidents of the Church and the peoples themselves have felt that in declaring the doctrine, the announcer was not ‘moved upon by the Holy Ghost,’” appear only in printed footnote 6. Second, the test Clark proposes is retrospective and communal — later Presidents and the membership decide — which is what makes the passage usable against teachings that were once taught from the same pulpit.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the hosted talk on churchofjesuschrist.org, including footnote 6, from which q2 is taken; the body of the talk carries only the second sentence of that quotation. Christofferson cites J. Reuben Clark Jr., “When Are Church Leaders' Words Entitled to Claim of Scripture?” Church News, July 31, 1954, 9–10. Included with the caveat that it is meta-level: no specific teaching on divine ancestry, spirit birth, or divine progression is named or softened here. What the entry records is the tool, not a use of it. RETREAT-REFRAME carries no stance by design — it describes an operation performed on earlier teaching rather than a position on any proposition.

title: Teachings of Presidents: Joseph Fielding Smith reprints the denial
speaker: Joseph Fielding Smith (curriculum reprint)
office: Teachings of Presidents of the Church series
venue: Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Joseph Fielding Smith (2013), ch. 1, “Our Father in Heaven”

quotes.excerpt: I am grateful that we know he is our Father in heaven, the Father of our spirits, and that he ordained the laws whereby we can advance and progress until we become like him. And I am grateful that we know he is an infinite and eternal being who knows all things and has all power and whose progression consists not in gaining more knowledge or power, not in further perfecting his godly attributes, but in the increase and multiplying of his kingdoms.
quotes.note: Denial, republished verbatim in current correlated curriculum — with the human-progression promise in the immediately preceding sentence. Human progression: affirmed; divine progression in knowledge: denied; the pairing in one paragraph is the modern settlement in miniature.

notes: Current Teachings of Presidents manual carrying the 1971 denial forward. Wording verified against the hosted manual text.

title: Elaine S. Dalton: “We are daughters of an exalted being!”
speaker: Elaine S. Dalton
office: Recently released Young Women General President
venue: General conference, Saturday morning session, April 2013 (Ensign, May 2013)

quotes.excerpt: No matter the language, each time I hear these words, “We are daughters of our Heavenly Father, who loves us, and we love Him,” the Spirit affirms to my soul that they are true. It is not only an affirmation of our identity—who we are—but also an acknowledgment of whose we are. We are daughters of an exalted being!
quotes.note: Exaltation predicated of the Father Himself, in the opening paragraph, as the payoff of unpacking the Young Women theme. Hedged rather than affirmed for two reasons: the phrase is adjectival (“an exalted being,” not “He attained exaltation”), and it is a single exclamation that the rest of the talk never returns to — the address is about virtue, covenant keeping, and acting well one's part. The counter-reading is live and is not foreclosed here: “exalted” may mean simply “most high.” Compare hunter-exalted-man-1948-q1, where the same construction is affirmed rather than hedged because Snow's couplet immediately supplies the mortality.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the hosted talk on churchofjesuschrist.org. Referent is the Father: the antecedent is the Young Women theme's “our Heavenly Father,” quoted in the same sentence. Included as a register datum — an outgoing general auxiliary president using exalted-being language of the Father in 2013 general conference, without hedge or footnote — while the note preserves the deflationary reading.

title: M. Russell Ballard: “our heavenly parents,” and a God and Christ “forever expanding Their light and glory”
speaker: M. Russell Ballard
office: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, Saturday morning session

quotes.excerpt: I then turned to the Pearl of Great Price and read again with wonder what the Lord God said to Moses: “And worlds without number have I created; and I also created them for mine own purpose; and by the Son I created them, which is mine Only Begotten” (Moses 1:33). … In our day the Hubble deep-space telescope has confirmed the magnitude of what Moses saw. Hubble scientists say the Milky Way galaxy, of which our earth and sun are just a tiny part, is estimated to be only one of over 200 billion similar galaxies.
quotes.note: Moses 1:33 read out and then corroborated from astronomy — plural worlds under one God, with the Son as the agent of creation. Nothing successive is claimed: no chain of Gods, no earlier creator, no suggestion that the worlds have other fathers. The elision between the scripture and the telescope is one intervening paragraph. Worth recording as the modern form of the many-worlds datum, in which the scripture is treated as an anticipated scientific result rather than as a cosmological claim with theological consequences — the opposite of what pratt-people-worlds-1871 does with the same premise.

quotes.excerpt: Just as a woman cannot conceive a child without a man, so a man cannot fully exercise the power of the priesthood to establish an eternal family without a woman. In other words, in the eternal perspective, both the procreative power and the priesthood power are shared by husband and wife.
quotes.note: Hedges, and the reason is grammatical rather than doctrinal. The analogy runs from mortal conception to priesthood, not the reverse; the conclusion generalizes the *sharing* of both powers, and “in the eternal perspective” modifies the sharing rather than the procreating. Read strictly, the sentence says that procreative power is jointly held, which is true of mortality, and leaves whether it continues past mortality to the hearer. It is nonetheless the address's closest approach to the generative claim, and it is characteristic of the correlated era that the approach is made through an argument about the standing of women rather than about eternity.

quotes.excerpt: Brothers and sisters, as the literal spirit children of our loving Heavenly Father, we have unlimited, divine potential.
quotes.note: Tagged on the fp-1916 precedent, where “the literal Parent … of the spirits of the human race” carries SPIRIT-BIRTH-VIVIPAROUS on the strength of the word literal alone. What Ballard asserts is literal descent; what he does not assert is any mechanism, and no Mother appears in this sentence — the parentage is the Father's only, four paragraphs before the sentence in which the parents go plural. The persistence of “literal” is the datum: it is the surviving lexical trace of fp-1909 and fp-1916 in current conference speech, doing the work of excluding an adoptive or figurative reading without stating what it affirms instead.

quotes.excerpt: And the primary purpose of this priesthood power is to bless, sanctify, and purify us so we can live together with our families in the presence of our heavenly parents, bound by priesthood sealings, participating in the marvelous work of God and Jesus Christ in forever expanding *Their* light and glory.
quotes.note: Two claims in one sentence, and the second is the unusual one. HEAVENLY-MOTHER: “our heavenly parents” in an Apostle's own voice, in a Saturday morning general session rather than a women's meeting — a plural that has become unremarkable by 2013 and would not have been in 1913. DIVINE-PROGRESSION, affirming: the light and glory of God and Jesus Christ are “forever expanding,” which is progression in dominion and glory rather than in knowledge, and is therefore the one form of it that jfs-progression-1971 and mcconkie-mormon-doctrine expressly permit — “they progress in the sense that their creations increase,” not in the sense that they learn. Recorded as an affirmation with that qualification stated rather than as a hedge, because the expansion is asserted flatly and forever. The italics on *Their* are the published text's, and they are the sentence's most interesting typography: the capital and the emphasis together make the plural pronoun refer to the Father and the Son, not to the heavenly parents named seven words earlier. The exalted are given a part in the expanding — “participating in the marvelous work” — which is as close as the address comes to a forward-chain claim, and it stops at participation.

notes: Quoted verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/2013/2013-04-ballard-this-is-my-work-and-glory.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; the live page was re-fetched during drafting on 2026-08-10 and returned the byline (“Elder M. Russell Ballard, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles”) and the opening of each excerpted sentence verbatim. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. Speaker disambiguation matters: this is M. Russell Ballard of the Twelve, not his great-grandfather Melvin J. Ballard, whose entries (ballard-increase, ballard-became-god-1914, ballard-couplet-narrowed-1917, mjballard-endless-increase-1929) sit a century earlier and say considerably more. The address is about priesthood power, and the eternal-increase material is entirely incidental to it, which is the point of filing it: four distinct axis-bearing sentences, none of them the subject, and no two of them in the same paragraph. The citesId edge is to moses-1 for the quotation of Moses 1:33; Moses 1:39 is also quoted later in the address.

title: Dallin H. Oaks, “No Other Gods” — “Our theology begins with heavenly parents”
speaker: Dallin H. Oaks
office: Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, Sunday morning session, October 2013 (Ensign, Nov. 2013)

quotes.excerpt: Knowledge of God's plan for His children gives Latter-day Saints a unique perspective on marriage and family. We are correctly known as a family-centered church. Our theology begins with heavenly parents, and our highest aspiration is to attain the fulness of eternal exaltation. We know this is possible only in a family relationship.
quotes.note: The most quotable modern apostolic statement of the structure: plural divine parentage is where the theology starts, and exaltation is reachable only inside a family. The euphemism tag is for the second half — “the fulness of eternal exaltation … only in a family relationship” places marriage on the causal path to exaltation without saying what marriage contributes there. Nothing in the sentence asserts new spirit children or a backward chain, and Oaks does not return to heavenly parents anywhere else in the talk.

quotes.excerpt: We look on marriage and the bearing and nurturing of children as part of God's plan and a sacred duty of those given the opportunity to do so. We believe that the ultimate treasures on earth and in heaven are our children and our posterity.
quotes.note: “And in heaven” is the load-bearing phrase — posterity is said to be a treasure past mortality, with nothing said about how one comes to have posterity there. Set beside the later sentence in section IV, “The power to create mortal life is the most exalted power God has given to His children,” whose careful word is *mortal*: the procreative claim in this talk is fenced to this life even as the posterity claim is not.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the hosted talk on churchofjesuschrist.org. Distinct from oaks-2019, which is the same speaker on the same axis six years later and does reach the “continuation of the seeds”; this 2013 address stops at heavenly parents plus relational exaltation. Filed as an original with no citation edges — the talk quotes no dataset text on this axis.

title: D&C and Church History Seminary Teacher Manual (2014), D&C 131–132 lesson
speaker: Church Educational System
office: Seminary curriculum (correlated)
venue: Seminary teacher manual

quotes.excerpt: “So far as the stages of eternal progression and attainment have been made known through divine revelation, we are to understand that only resurrected and glorified beings can become parents of spirit offspring. Only such exalted souls have reached maturity in the appointed course of eternal life; and the spirits born to them in the eternal worlds will pass in due sequence through the several stages or estates by which the glorified parents have attained exaltation” (“The Father and the Son…,” quoted in Ensign, Apr. 2002, 18).
quotes.note: Placeholder closed: the manual's spirit-offspring material is in Lesson 139 (D&C 132:3–33), which quotes the 1916 First Presidency exposition. The lesson also carries McConkie's Mormon Doctrine and Parley P. Pratt on the queen mother of “her numerous and still increasing offspring.”

quotes.excerpt: What do you think it means in verse 4 that if we are not sealed in the temple by the proper authority, we “cannot have an increase”? (To help students understand this verse, you may need to explain that increase refers to the opportunity to continue to have children in the celestial kingdom.)
quotes.note: Lesson 138 (D&C 131), in the teacher's own voice, and the exact 2014↔2025 measurement: this is the gloss on “increase” that the 2025 curriculum drops. Untagged — carried as the comparison datum rather than as evidence of a category.

notes: Superseded by the 2025 curriculum, hence discontinued. Note what the citation link makes visible: the manual supplies FORWARD-EXPLICIT language while citing a text this dataset rates as euphemism — the explicitness is added by the curriculum, not carried by the scripture. Paired with the 2025 entry, this is the collection's strongest original contribution.

title: Gospel Topics Essay, “Becoming Like God”
speaker: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (unsigned; First Presidency–approved)
office: Official essay
venue: churchofjesuschrist.org Gospel Topics Essays

quotes.excerpt: Little has been revealed about the first half of this couplet, and consequently little is taught.
quotes.note: Operation one, aimed at the Snow couplet: declare the backward half unrevealed. Note the move's dependence on the couplet's referent ambiguity — if the couplet is Christological, there is indeed little revealed, because it was never a claim about the Father.

quotes.excerpt: Latter-day Saints' doctrine of exaltation is often similarly reduced in media to a cartoonish image of people receiving their own planets.
quotes.note: Operation two: relocate deification into patristic theosis and ecumenical company (Irenaeus, C. S. Lewis), where neither regress nor spirit birth needs defending.

quotes.excerpt: “What kind of a being is God?” he asked… God “was once as one of us” and “all the spirits that God ever sent into the world” were likewise “susceptible of enlargement.” Joseph Smith preached that long before the world was formed, God found “himself in the midst” of these beings and “saw proper to institute laws whereby the rest could have a privilege to advance like himself” and be “exalted” with Him.
quotes.note: Operation three, and the essay's method in miniature: quote the historic teaching correctly, then frame it as undeveloped. The essay's handling is a mosaic of short quoted fragments in the body, not a block quotation, and the bracketing is done in footnote 19 rather than in the body: “While the King Follett discourse represents Joseph Smith’s most detailed known discussion of divine nature and exaltation, it is important to note that because of the wind on the day the sermon was delivered and the limitations of transcription techniques, we are left without certainty about Joseph Smith’s exact or complete wording during the sermon… But the surviving sermon text is not canonized and should not be treated as a doctrinal standard in and of itself.”

notes: Three quotes because the essay performs three distinct rhetorical operations on two different originals. Verify the excerpt wording against the current text, which has been lightly revised since 2014. Q1 (“Little has been revealed …”) verified verbatim against the currently hosted essay text, August 2026; q2 and q3 still need their wording checked.

title: Boyd K. Packer, “The Witness” — an apostolic promise that eternal increase will not be denied
speaker: Boyd K. Packer
office: President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, Sunday afternoon session, April 2014 (Ensign, May 2014)

quotes.excerpt: Parenthood is a sacred privilege, and depending upon faithfulness, it can be an eternal blessing.
quotes.note: Parenthood itself, not merely family association, is what is said to extend past mortality. The conditional — “depending upon faithfulness” — puts it on the exaltation track rather than making it a general promise.

quotes.excerpt: Those who do not marry or those who cannot have children are not excluded from the eternal blessings they seek but which, for now, remain beyond their reach. We do not always know how or when blessings will present themselves, but the promise of eternal increase will not be denied any faithful individual who makes and keeps sacred covenants.
quotes.note: Context supplies what the phrase will not: the audience is the unmarried and the childless, so “eternal increase” is being used to mean the posterity they do not have in mortality — but Packer states it as a promise rather than a description and never says what increase consists of after this life. He then reinforces it in his ordained capacity two paragraphs later (“As a servant of the Lord, acting in the office to which I have been ordained, I give those in such circumstances a promise …”), and the pastoral image he closes on is “Arms now empty will be filled.” Compare packer-parentage-1984, where the same speaker is explicit about spirit parentage; thirty years on, in general conference, the noun has dropped out.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the hosted talk on churchofjesuschrist.org. Packer's last general conference address on this axis; he died in July 2015. Filed as an original with no citation edges — the D&C 76 passage he reads at the close is his witness of Christ, not increase material.

title: Dieter F. Uchtdorf, “Living the Gospel Joyful” — the spirit-birth doctrine reaffirmed in a footnote
speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
office: Second Counselor in the First Presidency
venue: General Women's Session, October 2014 (Ensign, Nov. 2014)

quotes.excerpt: Pondering this truth—that we are children of heavenly parents—fills us with a sense of origin, purpose, and destiny.
quotes.note: The spoken text, carrying footnote 1. Plural parents affirmed; nothing about mechanism in the body of the talk, which repeats “daughter of God” and “your heavenly parents” in the pastoral register throughout.

quotes.excerpt: God is not only our Ruler and Creator; He is also our Heavenly Father. All men and women are literally the sons and daughters of God. President Joseph F. Smith taught that “man, as a spirit, was begotten and born of heavenly parents, and reared to maturity in the eternal mansions of the Father, prior to coming upon the earth in a temporal [physical] body”
quotes.note: Footnote 1 in full, and the whole reason this entry exists: begotten, born, reared to maturity — the viviparous account stated without hedge, in a document published over the name of a member of the First Presidency in 2014. The conflation caution is the placement. Nothing in this footnote is said aloud; the spoken sentence it hangs from says only “children of heavenly parents.” Anyone citing the talk for literal spirit birth is citing the printed apparatus, which is a real endorsement but not a pulpit statement.

quotes.excerpt: The promised blessings of God to the faithful are glorious and inspiring. Among them are “thrones, kingdoms, principalities, and powers, dominions, all heights and depths.” And it takes more than a spiritual birth certificate or a “Child of God Membership Card” to qualify for these incomprehensible blessings.
quotes.note: Unglossed scripture, and the interesting thing is where the quotation stops. Uchtdorf takes the dominions clause from D&C 132:19 and leaves the verse before it reaches “a continuation of the seeds forever and ever”; his later block quotation from the same section (verses 21–22, 24) is the strait-gate material, again avoiding the increase clause. He adds no interpretation of the blessings he names.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the hosted talk on churchofjesuschrist.org, footnotes included; q2 is footnote 1 in its entirety. The Joseph F. Smith sentence is quoted from Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Joseph F. Smith (1998), 335 — a manual with no dataset entry of its own, so no edge is drawn to it; the citesId edge is to D&C 132 for q3. Note the speaker distinction, since the two are routinely confused: this is Joseph F. Smith (sixth President), not Joseph Fielding Smith of tpjfs-2013.

title: D. Todd Christofferson, “Why Marriage, Why Family” — intelligences given form, not begotten
speaker: D. Todd Christofferson
office: Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, Saturday afternoon session, April 2015 (Ensign, May 2015)

quotes.excerpt: Prophets have revealed that we first existed as intelligences and that we were given form, or spirit bodies, by God, thus becoming His spirit children—sons and daughters of heavenly parents.
quotes.note: An organization account, not a birth account: the verb is “given form,” and spirit childhood is the *result* of that forming rather than of begetting. That is the minority reading in this corpus, and here it is stated by a member of the Twelve in general conference — set it beside uchtdorf-heavenly-parents-2014-q2, six months earlier, which reaffirms “begotten and born.” The tripartite tag is earned rather than retrojected: the talk stages intelligences, then spirit bodies, then a physical body “added upon” at mortality, in that order and with the transitions named.

quotes.excerpt: Thanks to our Heavenly Father, we had already become spirit beings. Now He was offering us a path to complete or perfect that being. The addition of the physical element is essential to the fulness of being and glory that God Himself enjoys.
quotes.note: The third stage, and the sentence that closes the loop back onto God: the physical element is “essential to the fulness of being and glory that God Himself enjoys,” which predicates embodiment of God without saying how He came by it. Included as the staging half of q1 rather than as a Father-axis claim — nothing here states attainment.

quotes.excerpt: Could we bridle the flesh so that it became the instrument rather than the master of the spirit? Could we be trusted both in time and eternity with godly powers, including power to create life?
quotes.note: “Both in time and eternity” extends the creative power past mortality, and “godly powers … power to create life” names it as God's own kind of power — but it is a rhetorical question about trustworthiness, and no object is ever given to the creating. Christofferson's fourth requirement of the plan, three paragraphs later, restricts itself carefully to mortal birth: God ordained “that men and women should marry and give birth to children, thereby creating, in partnership with God, the physical bodies that are key to the test of mortality.”

quotes.excerpt: “The first principles of man are self-existent with God. God himself, finding he was in the midst of spirits [or intelligences] and glory, because he was more intelligent, saw proper to institute laws whereby the rest could have a privilege to advance like himself. … He has power to institute laws to instruct the weaker intelligences, that they may be exalted with himself”
quotes.note: The King Follett Discourse, quoted in printed footnote 3 and cited to Teachings of Presidents of the Church: Joseph Smith (2007), 210. Recorded as context, not tagged: the passage is theosis — laws by which lesser intelligences advance and are exalted — and theosis alone is not a category here. Worth noting what is taken and what is left. Christofferson lifts the advance-like-himself and self-existent-intelligence material and quotes the phrase “could have a privilege to advance like himself” in the body of the talk, while the discourse's backward claims about God's own past go unmentioned.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the hosted talk on churchofjesuschrist.org, footnotes included; q4 is footnote 3, and the body of the talk quotes only its “could have a privilege to advance like himself” clause. Citation edges: kfd-1844 for that quotation, proclamation-1995 for the warning Christofferson quotes about the disintegration of the family. The entry's value is the mechanism split — an apostolic organization account of spirit origin in 2015, one conference after a First Presidency footnote reaffirming literal begetting.

title: Boyd K. Packer, “The Plan of Happiness” — the procreative power as the road to “even godhood”
speaker: Boyd K. Packer
office: President of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, Saturday morning session, April 2015, Salt Lake City

quotes.excerpt: The commandment to multiply and replenish the earth has never been rescinded. It is essential to the plan of redemption and is the source of human happiness. Through the righteous exercise of this power, we may come close to our Father in Heaven and experience a fulness of joy, even godhood. The power of procreation is not an incidental part of the plan; it is the plan of happiness; it is the key to happiness.
quotes.note: The sentence this entry exists for, and the strongest twenty-first-century conference statement of the mechanism: it is the procreative power itself, righteously exercised, that brings “a fulness of joy, even godhood.” Rated euphemism rather than explicit on the v2 no-retrojection rule — deification is named outright, and the means is named outright, but the object never is. Nothing here says the exalted beget. What it says is that the power by which mortals beget is the power by which they become gods, which is the premise of the generative claim with the conclusion left off. Note also the register: this is a talk about chastity, and the godhood clause arrives as a subordinate reason for keeping the law.

quotes.excerpt: When entered into worthily, this process combines the most exquisite and exalted physical, emotional, and spiritual feelings associated with the word love. That part of life has no equal, no counterpart, in all human experience. It will, when covenants are made and kept, last eternally, “for therein are the keys of the holy priesthood ordained, that you may receive honor and glory” (D&C 124:34), “which glory shall be a fulness and a continuation of the seeds forever and ever” (D&C 132:19).
quotes.note: The D&C 132:19 code phrase quoted with no gloss whatever — the speaker adds nothing to “continuation of the seeds forever and ever.” What distinguishes this instance from oaks-2019-q1 and carpenter-2024-q1, which deploy the same phrase the same way, is the antecedent: the “It” that will “last eternally” is marital sexual union, named two sentences earlier. The adjacency is as tight as it gets in current correlated speech without becoming a statement. Italics on the word love are the published text's.

quotes.excerpt: He will tempt, if he can, to degrade, to corrupt, and, if possible, to destroy this gift by which we may, if we are worthy, have eternal increase (see D&C 132:28–31).
quotes.note: The technical term itself — “eternal increase” — deployed in general conference in 2015 and left undefined, with the citation pointing back into D&C 132. Compare oaks-eternal-increase-2018-q1, where the same apostolic body uses the same phrase three years later of children born in mortality; here the referent is a promised future blessing conditioned on worthiness, which is the older sense.

quotes.excerpt: The Gods went down to organize man in their own image, in the image of the Gods to form they him, male and female to form they them. … And the Gods said: We will cause them to be fruitful and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it
quotes.note: Untagged. Packer opens the doctrinal section by reading Abraham 4:27–28 aloud, plural “the Gods” and all, and adds no comment on the plural — the scripture is used to establish the male-and-female creation and the multiply commandment, not a plurality of divine beings. Recorded because this dataset's question is partly about what passes unremarked in correlated speech, and a plurality-of-Gods text read from the general conference pulpit in 2015 without a gloss is a datum of exactly that kind. No category applies: the schema has no plurality tag, and reading one in would be retrojection.

quotes.excerpt: Love is nourished by the coming of children, who spring from that fountain of life entrusted to couples in marriage. … A child comes forth in the miracle of birth, created in the image of its earthly father and mother. Within its mortal body is a spirit able to feel and perceive spiritual things. Dormant in that mortal body of this child is the power to beget offspring in its own image.
quotes.note: Untagged context, kept because it supplies the pattern the talk runs on: begetting in one's own image, generation after generation, presented as the created order. Every clause is about mortal birth. The premortal and postmortal extensions that nineteenth-century speakers drew from the same pattern (see young-celestial-bodies-1876, pratt-people-worlds-1871) are not drawn here.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page, which was fetched during drafting and returned every excerpted paragraph verbatim; the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/2015/2015-04-packer-the-plan-of-happiness.md carries a heavyweight pass diffing its body against the same page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. Packer's last general conference address, delivered three months before his death. The entry's value is that all four components of the historic generative claim appear in a single fifteen-minute talk — procreative power as the means of godhood, the D&C 132:19 seeds phrase, the term “eternal increase,” and a plural-Gods creation text — and the talk never joins them into the proposition that exalted couples beget spirit children. Tagged euphemism throughout for that reason. Read with reeves-promised-blessings-2015, which rebroadcasts the godhood sentence in the next general conference with a bracketed editorial gloss, and with packer-parentage-1984, where the same speaker thirty-one years earlier deflates plurality of Gods to the arithmetic of the Godhead.

title: Gospel Topics Essay, “Mother in Heaven”
speaker: Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (unsigned; First Presidency–approved)
office: Official essay
venue: churchofjesuschrist.org Gospel Topics Essays

quotes.excerpt: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints teaches that all human beings, male and female, are beloved spirit children of heavenly parents, a Heavenly Father and a Heavenly Mother.
quotes.note: Affirmation without mechanism.

notes: The citation link now makes the observation machine-visible: this essay cites the 1909 statement while declining to reproduce its “begotten and born” language. The gap between what is cited and what is quoted is a precise measure of the reframe.

title: Linda S. Reeves rebroadcasts Packer's “even godhood” — with a bracket
speaker: Linda S. Reeves
office: Second Counselor in the Relief Society General Presidency
venue: General conference, general women's session, October 2015, Salt Lake City

quotes.excerpt: In President Boyd K. Packer’s final general conference talk, which you may remember as “a cookie and a kiss,” he testified that “the commandment to multiply and replenish the earth … is essential … and is the source of human happiness. Through the righteous exercise of this [creative] power, we may come close to our Father in Heaven and experience a fulness of joy, even godhood. The power of procreation is not an incidental part of the plan; it is the plan.”
quotes.note: The doctrinal content is Packer's, quoted approvingly six months after he gave it (see packer-plan-of-happiness-2015-q1); Reeves formulates nothing new. Two editorial changes are the reason this is worth its own entry. First, the bracket: “this [creative] power” supplies an antecedent Packer's sentence carried by context, and the word chosen is creative — the same vocabulary Oaks uses in 2019 (“the creative powers inherent in the combination of male and female”) and Renlund in 2020. Second, the truncation: Packer's “it is the plan of happiness; it is the key to happiness” is cut to “it is the plan.” Both changes tighten the claim rather than soften it. Ellipses inside the quotation are Reeves's own, as printed.

quotes.excerpt: Our bodies are sacred gifts from our Heavenly Father. They are personal temples. As we keep them clean and pure, we can be worthy to help our Heavenly Father create bodies for His beloved spirit children.
quotes.note: Marked implied, on the same reading given proclamation-1995-q1: God's spirit children are presupposed, and nothing is said about how they came to be His. The direction is backward rather than forward — this is about the spirits already waiting, not about offspring the exalted will have — and the only mechanism named is the mortal one, in which parents furnish bodies. Earlier in the talk the same picture appears in devotional register: “this celestial spirit, so recently sent by our Father in Heaven to its newly created, pure little body.” No Mother appears anywhere in the address.

quotes.excerpt: I testify that our bodies are sacred gifts from our Heavenly Father and that as we keep our lives pure and clean through the atoning sacrifice of our Savior and keep the vision of our Father’s promised rewards daily in front of us, we will one day receive “all that [our] Father hath.”
quotes.note: The closing sentence, and the D&C 84:38 inheritance formula in its standard modern use — maximal in scope, unspecified in content. Identical in function to renlund-divine-nature-2022-q6 (“receive all that He has. He cannot offer you more”). The published footnote points to Doctrine and Covenants 84:38.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the live page, which returned all three excerpts verbatim; the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/2015/2015-10-reeves-worthy-of-our-promised-blessings.md carries a 1.0000 heavyweight diff against the same page. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. Filed as a citation because the load-bearing doctrinal sentence is Packer's, not Reeves's — the collapse-to-originals view should fold q1 into packer-plan-of-happiness-2015. What the entry records that the original does not is the reception: the “even godhood” sentence was not a one-off, it was selected for rebroadcast to the women of the Church in the next conference, by a member of a general presidency, with an editorial bracket that makes its referent more explicit rather than less.

title: Jeffrey R. Holland thanks “a Mother in Heaven” from the general conference pulpit
speaker: Jeffrey R. Holland
office: Of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles
venue: General conference, Saturday afternoon session, Salt Lake City

quotes.excerpt: To Mother Eve, to Sarah, Rebekah, and Rachel, to Mary of Nazareth, and to a Mother in Heaven, I say, “Thank you for your crucial role in fulfilling the purposes of eternity.”
quotes.note: Affirmation by address rather than by assertion — Holland does not say she exists, he thanks her, which presupposes it more strongly than a proposition would. Two features are worth keeping. She is the last item in a list of scriptural women, so her existence is carried on the same grammatical footing as Eve's and Mary's and requires no separate warrant. And the thanks names a function: “your crucial role in fulfilling the purposes of eternity,” which is more than hinckley-daughters-of-god-1991 conceded and closer to maxwell-heavenly-mother-1978's Mother who makes arrangements. Still nothing about what the role is. The indefinite article — “a Mother in Heaven” — is the published reading.

quotes.excerpt: Today I declare from this pulpit what has been said here before: that no love in mortality comes closer to approximating the pure love of Jesus Christ than the selfless love a devoted mother has for her child.
quotes.note: Untagged context, and the interpretive key to the address. The sermon's argument is analogical throughout — maternal bearing, carrying and delivering as the nearest mortal approximation of the Atonement — so by the time the closing sentence reaches a Mother in Heaven, the audience has spent fifteen minutes being taught to read motherhood as a window onto deity. Whether that makes the closing thanks doctrinal or rhetorical is exactly the question the entry leaves open; what is not in question is that the sentence was spoken, in general conference, and printed.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/2015/2015-10-holland-behold-thy-mother.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; the closing sentence was independently re-fetched from the live page during drafting and returned verbatim. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. The timing is the fact to record and it is tighter than usual: the Gospel Topics essay on Mother in Heaven (essay-2015) was published in October 2015, the same month as this address, and the two are the Church's paired statements of that moment — an essay that says what is known, and an apostle who addresses her directly in front of the whole Church without saying anything further about her. Read against renlund-divine-nature-2022 seven years later, where the same combination is made explicit as policy: the doctrine is revealed, the content is a Gospel Library page, and speculation is out.

title: Henry B. Eyring: “the promise of an endless posterity”
speaker: Henry B. Eyring
office: First Counselor in the First Presidency
venue: General conference, general priesthood session, April 2016, Salt Lake City

quotes.excerpt: Before we were born, we lived in a family with our exalted and eternal Heavenly Father. He ordained a plan that enables us to advance and progress to become like Him. He did it out of love for us. The purpose of the plan was to allow us the privilege of living forever as our Heavenly Father lives. … Eternal life is that kind of life which God our Eternal Father lives.
quotes.note: The “kind of life God lives” formula, twice in adjacent paragraphs, and the frame the closing promise depends on. Compare gospel-principles-2011, where the same phrase is the term that gets defined as including spirit-parenthood, and renlund-2020-q3, where it is left undefined. Eyring leaves it undefined. One precision point against retrojection: “our exalted and eternal Heavenly Father” is not tagged for the Father's status. Paired with “eternal,” exalted here reads as an honorific describing His present state, not as a claim that He attained it — contrast alliaud-exalted-man-2024-q1, where “is an exalted man” is quoted from Joseph Smith as a statement about what God is.

quotes.excerpt: Among those “many things” is the promise of an endless posterity. My prayer is that we may all qualify and help others to qualify for that supernal blessing in the home of our Father and His Beloved Son, Jesus Christ.
quotes.note: The last two sentences of the address, glossing Matthew 25:21's “I will make thee ruler over many things.” Rated euphemism rather than explicit on the eternal-family-2022-q2 precedent: “posterity” does not discriminate spirit offspring begotten after exaltation from a sealed mortal line extended forever, and the modifier doing the work is “endless,” which is about duration and number rather than about kind. What makes it worth recording is placement and speaker — a member of the First Presidency naming endless posterity, not exaltation or eternal life generally, as the supernal blessing priesthood holders should qualify for, in the final sentence of a priesthood session address.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the live page, which returned both excerpts verbatim; the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/2016/2016-04-eyring-eternal-families.md carries a 1.0000 heavyweight diff against the same page. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. Filed as an original: the phrase is Eyring's own, not a quotation. No citesId — the address quotes Joseph Smith, Bruce R. McConkie's April 1970 conference report, N. Eldon Tanner and Harold B. Lee, but none of those passages are entries in this dataset and the McConkie item cited (Conference Report, Apr. 1970, 26–27, on creating and perfecting an eternal family unit) is not the “family affair” hymn discourse recorded at mcconkie-family-affair-1970. Note the elision in q1 is this dataset's, marking the paragraph break between the two “kind of life” statements.

title: Donald L. Hallstrom, “I Am a Child of God” — the proof-text set for literal divine parentage
speaker: Donald L. Hallstrom
office: Of the Presidency of the Seventy
venue: General conference, Saturday morning session, April 2016, Salt Lake City

quotes.excerpt: Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon received a vision in which they saw the Father and the Son, and a heavenly voice declared that the inhabitants of the worlds “are begotten sons and daughters unto God.” … In 1995, the 15 living apostles and prophets affirmed: “All human beings … are created in the image of God. Each is a beloved spirit son or daughter of heavenly parents.”
quotes.note: Two items from a six-item bulleted proof-text list (Moses 1:13; Psalm 82:6; Acts 17:29; D&C 76:24; the family proclamation; Thomas S. Monson), reproduced here because they are the two that carry generative or plural-parent content. Both are quotations, and Hallstrom adds no gloss to either: D&C 76:24's “begotten sons and daughters unto God” is read straight off the page as a statement of our divine parentage, with no comment on what “begotten” means or on the verse's own context, in which the begetting is by Christ; and “heavenly parents” arrives inside the proclamation sentence rather than as a claim of his own — the Mother is never mentioned in the address in his own voice. Marked implied for both tags accordingly, and rated hedges on the spirit-birth axis on the proclamation-1995-q1 reading: literal parentage presumed, generation unstated. The ellipses are the published text's, except the one joining the two bullets, which is this dataset's.

quotes.excerpt: This doctrine is so basic, so oft stated, and so instinctively simple that it can seem to be ordinary, when in reality it is among the most extraordinary knowledge we can obtain. A correct understanding of our heavenly heritage is essential to exaltation.
quotes.note: Untagged, and untagged deliberately. Divine parentage is here made the Church's “most fundamental doctrine” and a precondition of exaltation — a maximal claim about its importance that contains no claim at all about its content. Nothing is said about the Father's own parentage, about progression, or about what the exalted do; the whole talk asserts our divine descent and stops. Recorded because the shape is characteristic: the doctrine is elevated in status at the same time as it is emptied of the cosmology that once surrounded it. Compare packer-parentage-1984-q4, untagged for the same reason.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the live page, which returned both excerpts and the surrounding bullets verbatim; the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/2016/2016-04-hallstrom-i-am-a-child-of-god.md carries a 1.0000 heavyweight diff against the same page. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. Filed as an original with a single citesId edge to the family proclamation; no edge to D&C 76, which has no entry in this dataset. The conflation caution belongs at the top of any use of this entry: Hallstrom asserts our divine parentage and nothing whatever about God the Father's own origin, mortality, or progression — this is category A with a literal-descent premise, not category C, and it should not be counted toward the backward axis in either direction.

title: Neill F. Marriott: “more like our Father and Mother in heaven,” and becoming like heavenly parents
speaker: Neill F. Marriott
office: Second Counselor in the Young Women General Presidency
venue: General conference, general women's session, April 2016, Salt Lake City

quotes.excerpt: Elder Orson F. Whitney wrote: “All that we suffer and all that we endure, especially when we endure it patiently, … purifies our hearts … and makes us more tender and charitable, … and it is through … toil and tribulation, that we gain the education … which will make us more like our Father and Mother in heaven.”
quotes.note: The fourth and latest general conference appearance of the Whitney adversity passage, and graded C on its own for the reason set out at howard-hunter-whitney-1987-q1: the published footnote sources it only to “Orson F. Whitney, in Spencer W. Kimball, Faith Precedes the Miracle (1972), 98,” a devotional paperback that itself prints the passage without a citation, so the chain is Whitney (d. 1931) → Kimball's uncited book → the pulpit. Marriott's version trims the passage with four ellipses, all printed in the published text, and keeps the “Father and Mother in heaven” clause intact. Likeness, not generation — nothing here asserts a mechanism.

quotes.excerpt: As we ask Father in Heaven to make us builders of His kingdom, His power will flow into us and we will know how to nurture, ultimately becoming like our heavenly parents.
quotes.note: The last sentence of the address, and the reason this entry exists apart from the Whitney lineage: here the plural parents are in Marriott's own voice, not inside a quotation, and they are the terminus of the talk's argument about nurture. Lowercase “heavenly parents” as printed. Still likeness rather than generation — the verb is becoming like, and the talk's account of what mothering is (“I believe that ‘to mother’ means ‘to give life’,” extended to emotional and spiritual life) is explicitly broadened past childbearing rather than extended past mortality.

notes: Verified 2026-08-10 against the live page, which returned both excerpts verbatim; the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/2016/2016-04-marriott-what-shall-we-do.md carries a 1.0000 heavyweight diff against the same page. Official published text, so A at entry level, with the Whitney quotation graded C — see the quote note. Filed as an original with no citesId: the Whitney text has no entry in this dataset, and whitney-father-and-mother-1907 is a different address making a different argument and must not be used as the target. Curatorial flag for whoever merges this: q1 duplicates material already documented inside the notes of howard-hunter-whitney-1987, which states that the Komatsu and Marriott instances are recorded there rather than drafted as entries of their own. Drafted here anyway because q2 is Marriott's own and is not recorded anywhere in the dataset; if the curator prefers the earlier decision, the right resolution is to drop q1 and keep this entry for q2, not to drop the entry.

title: Dieter F. Uchtdorf: “eternal beings, without beginning” who are “the literal spirit children” of Heavenly Parents
speaker: Dieter F. Uchtdorf
office: Second Counselor in the First Presidency
venue: General conference, Saturday morning session, Salt Lake City

quotes.excerpt: Brothers and sisters, we are eternal beings, without beginning and without end. We have always existed. We are the literal spirit children of divine, immortal, and omnipotent Heavenly Parents!
quotes.note: Affirmation, from the First Presidency, capitalized and exclaimed. Two other things are happening in the same three sentences and neither is tagged. First, the eternity claim and the literal-childhood claim are set side by side with no transition between them — the published footnote on “We have always existed” is D&C 93:29, the uncreated-intelligence verse — so the passage states the two ends of the tripartite model without ever staging the middle; per the category definition, TRIPARTITE-FRAMEWORK is reserved for sources that actually articulate three stages, and there is no verb here that moves anyone from one to the next. Second, “literal spirit children” asserts real parentage and says nothing about how, which is the same discipline applied at kimball-intelligence-spirit-form-1978, so no SPIRIT-BIRTH tag attaches in either direction. What survives from fp-1909 is the word literal; what does not is “begotten and born.”

quotes.excerpt: I remember trying to draw the plan of salvation on a blackboard in a classroom of our chapel in Frankfurt, Germany. I made circles that represented premortal life, mortality, and the return to our Heavenly Parents after this life.
quotes.note: The same plural, thirteen paragraphs earlier and in a wholly different register — a teenager's chalk diagram in Frankfurt, recalled as the thing that finally got his friends' attention. Recorded because it dates the vocabulary to the speaker's own youth and shows the plural functioning as ordinary catechesis rather than as a doctrinal assertion under pressure. Uchtdorf's frame for the whole address is that Latter-day Saints have stopped noticing what they hold (“we teach them to our three-year-olds in the Sunbeam class”), which is the most accurate available description of how Heavenly Parents language travels in the modern corpus: everywhere, unargued, and never elaborated.

notes: Re-pulled verbatim from the Pulpit vault file talks/english/modern/2016/2016-10-uchtdorf-o-how-great-the-plan-of-our-god.md, whose heavyweight pass diffed the vault body against the live churchofjesuschrist.org page paragraph by paragraph at a 1.0000 match; both passages were independently re-fetched from the live page during drafting and returned verbatim. Official published text, so A, and still hosted, so current-correlated. The vault carries the published footnote markers; they are dropped from the excerpts and their content is described in the quote notes.
